sentences.zh: 文苑二

translations.literal: Literary Grove Two.
translations.idiomatic: Literary Grove, Part Two.

sentences.zh: ○高頔李度韓溥鞠常宋準柳開夏侯嘉正羅處約安德裕錢熙

translations.literal: Gao Di, Li Du, Han Pu, Ju Chang, Song Zhun, Liu Kai, Xia Houjiazheng, Luo Chuyue, An Deyu, and Qian Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Di, Li Du, Han Pu, Ju Chang, Song Zhun, Liu Kai, Xia Houjiazheng, Luo Chuyue, An Deyu, and Qian Xi.

sentences.zh: 高頔字子奇，開封雍丘人。

translations.literal: Gao Di, styled Ziqi, was a native of Yongqiu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Di, styled Ziqi, came from Yongqiu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 後唐清泰中舉進士，同輩紿之曰：「何不從裴僕射求知乎？」

translations.literal: During Qingtai of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination. His peers deceived him, saying: "Why not seek a letter of recommendation from Vice Censor Pei?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination. His fellow candidates tricked him, saying, "Why not ask Vice Censor Pei for a letter of recommendation?"

sentences.zh: 時裴皞以左僕射致仕，後進無至其門者。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Hao had retired as Left Vice Censor, and no younger scholars came to his door.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Pei Hao had retired from his post as Left Vice Censor, and no younger scholars ever called on him.

sentences.zh: 頔性純樸，信其言，以文贄於皞。

translations.literal: Di was by nature simple and honest; he believed their words and presented a literary gift to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Di was plain and guileless by nature. He took them at their word and presented a literary gift to Pei Hao.

sentences.zh: 明年，禮部侍郎馬裔孫知貢舉，乃皞門下生也。

translations.literal: The following year, Ma Yisun, Vice Minister of Rites, supervised the examinations; he was a disciple under Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ma Yisun, Vice Minister of Rites, supervised the examinations. He had been a disciple of Pei Hao.

sentences.zh: 皞以頔語之，遂擢乙科，四遷魏博觀察支使。

translations.literal: Hao spoke of Di to him, and he was promoted to the second rank; after four promotions he became administrative aide to the Weibo Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hao spoke of Di to him, and Di was placed in the second rank. After four promotions he became administrative aide to the Weibo Observation Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，符彥卿奏署掌書記。

translations.literal: During Xiande of Zhou, Fu Yanqing memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era of Zhou, Fu Yanqing memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 時太宗親迎懿德皇后於大名，彥卿遣頔迎候，日夕陪接，尤伸款好。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Taizong personally went to Daming to welcome Empress Yide; Yanqing dispatched Di to greet and receive him. Day and night Di attended him, and they especially extended warm friendship.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Taizong went in person to Daming to welcome Empress Yide. Yanqing sent Di to greet him, and Di attended him day and night, drawing especially close in mutual regard.

sentences.zh: 後隨彥卿鎮鳳翔，會詔留彥卿洛陽，頔復為天雄軍掌書記。

translations.literal: Later he followed Yanqing to command at Fengxiang. When an edict ordered Yanqing to remain at Luoyang, Di again served as chief secretary of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Yanqing to his command at Fengxiang. When an edict ordered Yanqing to remain at Luoyang, Di again served as chief secretary of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 後以病免，居於魏。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed due to illness and lived in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later he resigned on account of illness and settled in Wei.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，太宗親試貢士，頔子南金舉學究，自陳曰：「臣父年八十四，嘗佐使幕，久已罷職，家貧無以存養。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Taizong personally examined tribute scholars. Di's son Nanjin entered for the xueju degree and stated himself: "My father is eighty-four years old. He once served on a commissioner staff, but has long been dismissed from office. Our family is poor and unable to support him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Taizong personally examined tribute scholars. Di's son Nanjin entered for the xueju degree and declared: "My father is eighty-four. He once served on a commissioner staff but has long been out of office. Our family is poor and cannot support him.

sentences.zh: 願賜一第，庶獲寸祿，以及老父。」

translations.literal: I hope to be granted one rank, that I may obtain even a small stipend to support my aged father."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be granted a degree, that I may receive even a modest stipend and provide for my aged father."

sentences.zh: 上問左右其父何人，宰相宋琪以頔對，且言其素行廉介，老而彌厲，甚為搢紳推重。

translations.literal: The emperor asked those around him who his father was. Chief Minister Song Qi answered with Di and said that his conduct had always been incorruptible, and in old age he was all the more strict—greatly respected among the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked those around him who the father was. Chief Minister Song Qi named Gao Di and said that his conduct had always been incorruptible and grew only stricter with age, and that the gentry held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此高頔子耶！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Is this the son of Gao Di!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is the son of Gao Di!

sentences.zh: 頔在大名幕中，嘗與朕遊處，迨逾旬月。

translations.literal: Di was in the staff at Daming and once kept company with me for more than ten days and a month.
translations.idiomatic: Di was on the staff at Daming and once kept company with me for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 晨暮對案飲食，常拱手危坐，未曾少懈，其恭謹蓋天性也。

translations.literal: Morning and evening at meals across the table, he always sat upright with hands folded and never relaxed in the least—such respectful diligence was evidently in his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening at meals across the table he always sat upright with hands folded and never once slackened. Such respectful diligence was plainly in his nature.

sentences.zh: 惜其老矣，不欲煩以官政。」

translations.literal: It is a pity he is old; I do not wish to burden him with official duties."
translations.idiomatic: It is a pity he is old; I do not wish to burden him with official duties."

sentences.zh: 即擢南金第，拜頔左補闕致仕，賜錢十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Nanjin was granted a rank; Di was appointed Left Remonstrator with retirement status and given a hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Nanjin was granted a degree. Di was appointed Left Remonstrator with retirement status and given a hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home.

sentences.zh: 頔有清節，力學強記，手寫書千餘卷。

translations.literal: Di had a reputation for upright integrity, studied diligently with a powerful memory, and hand-copied more than a thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: Di was known for upright integrity. He studied hard, had a formidable memory, and hand-copied more than a thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 彥卿待之甚厚，或過致優給，頔計口受費，餘皆不納。

translations.literal: Yanqing treated him very generously; sometimes he sent extra provisions, but Di calculated per mouth the amount he needed and accepted nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing treated him very generously and sometimes sent extra provisions, but Di calculated what he needed per mouth and would accept nothing beyond that.

sentences.zh: 彥卿左右多肆貪虐，民不能堪，及彥卿罷鎮，其故時將吏、賓客皆心愧，無敢復遊魏者。

translations.literal: Many of Yanqing's attendants were greedy and cruel, and the people could not endure it. When Yanqing left his post, his former officers and guests all felt ashamed in their hearts, and none dared again to visit Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Yanqing's attendants were greedy and cruel, and the people could not bear it. When Yanqing left his command, his former officers and guests all felt ashamed, and none dared visit Wei again.

sentences.zh: 惟頔清苦守法，魏人愛之。

translations.literal: Only Di lived in hardship yet kept the law; the people of Wei loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Di lived in hardship yet kept the law, and the people of Wei loved him.

sentences.zh: 在魏三十年，無一人言其非者。

translations.literal: For thirty years in Wei, not a single person spoke ill of him.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years in Wei, not one person spoke ill of him.

sentences.zh: 所乘馬老，以糜飼之。

translations.literal: The horse he rode was old; he fed it with grain porridge.
translations.idiomatic: The horse he rode was old, and he fed it with grain porridge.

sentences.zh: 仆夫年七十，待之如初，時稱其長者。

translations.literal: His servant was seventy years old; he treated him as when he first hired him. The times called him a man of exemplary character.
translations.idiomatic: His servant was seventy, yet he treated him as he had from the first. People of the time called him a man of exemplary character.

sentences.zh: 次子鼎，舉進士，至殿中丞。

translations.literal: His second son Ding passed the jinshi examination and reached the position of Director in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Ding passed the jinshi examination and rose to the post of Director in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李度，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Li Du was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Du came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中舉進士。

translations.literal: During Xiande of Zhou he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era of Zhou he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 度工於詩，有「醉輕浮世事，老重故鄉人」之句。

translations.literal: Du was skilled at poetry and had the lines: "In drunkenness worldly affairs seem light; in old age one holds dear the people of one's hometown."
translations.idiomatic: Du was skilled at poetry and had the lines, "In drunkenness worldly affairs seem light; in old age one holds dear the people of one's hometown."

sentences.zh: 時翰林學士申文炳知貢舉，樞密使王樸移書錄其句以薦之，文炳即擢度為第三人。

translations.literal: At that time Hanlin Academician Shen Wenbing supervised the examinations. Privy Councilor Wang Pu sent a letter quoting his lines to recommend him, and Wenbing immediately ranked Du third.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hanlin Academician Shen Wenbing supervised the examinations. Privy Councilor Wang Pu sent a letter quoting Du's lines to recommend him, and Wenbing immediately ranked Du third.

sentences.zh: 釋褐永寧縣主簿。

translations.literal: Upon entering office he became chief clerk of Yongning County.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he became chief clerk of Yongning County.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中丞、知歙州。

translations.literal: After successive promotions he became Director in the Palace Secretariat and prefect of She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After successive promotions he became Director in the Palace Secretariat and prefect of She Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐事左遷絳州團練使，十年不調。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to regimental commissioner of Jiang Prefecture and received no new appointment for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to regimental commissioner of Jiang Prefecture and received no new appointment for ten years.

sentences.zh: 度在歙州，嘗以所著詩刻於石，有中黃門得其石本，傳入禁中，太宗見之，謂宰相曰：「度今安在？」

translations.literal: While Du was in She Prefecture, he once had his poems carved on stone. A middle palace eunuch obtained a rubbing and it reached the inner palace. Emperor Taizong saw it and said to the chief ministers: "Where is Du now?"
translations.idiomatic: While Du was in She Prefecture, he once had his poems carved on stone. A middle palace eunuch obtained a rubbing and it reached the inner palace. Emperor Taizong saw it and asked the chief ministers, "Where is Du now?"

sentences.zh: 即令召至，對於便殿，與語甚悅，擢為虞部員外郎、直史館，賜緋。

translations.literal: He was immediately summoned and received in the informal hall. The emperor was greatly pleased in conversation and promoted him to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, assigned to the Historiography Institute, and granted scarlet robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately summoned and received in the informal hall. The emperor was greatly pleased in conversation and promoted him to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, assigned him to the Historiography Institute, and granted him scarlet robes.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，籍田畢，交州黎桓加恩，命度借太常少卿充官告國信副使，上賜詩以寵行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, after the plowing ceremony, Li Huan of Jiaozhou was granted honors. Du was ordered to serve temporarily as Vice Director of the Ministry of Ritual and deputy envoy bearing the imperial patent and credentials; the emperor granted him a poem to honor his departure.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duangong era, after the plowing ceremony, Li Huan of Jiaozhou was granted honors. Du was ordered to serve temporarily as Vice Director of the Ministry of Ritual and deputy envoy bearing the imperial patent and credentials, and the emperor granted him a poem to honor his departure.

sentences.zh: 未至交州，卒於太平軍傳舍，年五十七。

translations.literal: Before reaching Jiaozhou he died at a relay station in Taiping Army, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching Jiaozhou he died at a relay station in Taiping Army, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 度之南使，每至州府，即借圖經觀其勝跡，皆形篇詩，以上所賜詩有「奉使南遊多好景」之句，遂題為《奉使南遊集》，未成編而亡。

translations.literal: On Du's mission south, whenever he reached a prefecture or district he borrowed local gazetteers to view famous sites, and all were given form in poems. Because the poem granted by the emperor had the line "On mission to the south, many fine vistas," he titled the collection 《Collection of a Mission Journey South》, but it was never compiled before he died.
translations.idiomatic: On Du's mission south, whenever he reached a prefecture or district he borrowed local gazetteers to view famous sites and turned each into a poem. Because the poem the emperor had granted him contained the line "On mission to the south, many fine vistas," he titled the collection 《Collection of a Mission Journey South》, but it was never compiled before he died.

sentences.zh: 弟康亦善詩，太平興國二年，登進士第，官至太子右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: His younger brother Kang was also skilled at poetry. In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and reached the office of Right Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kang was also skilled at poetry. In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and rose to the office of Right Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 韓溥，京兆長安人，唐相休之裔孫。

translations.literal: Han Pu was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao, a descendant of Tang chief minister Han Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Pu came from Chang'an in Jingzhao and was a descendant of Tang chief minister Han Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 少俊敏，善屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and quick, skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was clever and quick and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初舉進士，累遷曆使府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande of Zhou he passed the jinshi examination and through successive promotions served in various commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiande era of Zhou he passed the jinshi examination and through successive promotions served in various commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，自靜難軍掌書記召為監察御史，三遷至庫部員外郎、知華州，同判靈州，再轉司門郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he was summoned from chief secretary of the Jingnan Army to serve as investigating censor. After three promotions he became Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, prefect of Hua Prefecture, concurrently judging Ling Prefecture, and then transferred again to Director in the Ministry of Revenues.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao he was summoned from chief secretary of the Jingnan Army to serve as investigating censor. After three promotions he became Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, prefect of Hua Prefecture, concurrently judging Ling Prefecture, and then transferred again to Director in the Ministry of Revenues.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年被病，表請辭職尋醫，許之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he fell ill, memorialized requesting leave to resign and seek treatment, and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he fell ill, memorialized requesting leave to resign and seek treatment, and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 溥博學善持論，詳練台閣故事，多知唐朝氏族，與人談亹然可聽，號為「近世肉譜」，搢紳頗推重之。

translations.literal: Pu was broadly learned and skilled at argument, thoroughly versed in the precedents of the central administration, and knew much about Tang clans. When speaking with others he was engaging to listen to; he was called the "living genealogy of recent times," and the gentry greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was broadly learned and skilled at argument, thoroughly versed in the precedents of the central administration, and knew much about Tang clans. When he spoke with others he was engaging to listen to. He was called the "living genealogy of recent times," and the gentry greatly respected him.

sentences.zh: 尤善筆劄，人多藏尺牘。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at letters; many people collected his writings.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at letters, and many people collected his writings.

sentences.zh: 弟洎，亦進士及第。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ji also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ji also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 鞠常，字可久，密州高密人。

translations.literal: Ju Chang, styled Kejiu, was a native of Gaomi in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Chang, styled Kejiu, came from Gaomi in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖真，黃縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was magistrate of Huang County.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen was magistrate of Huang County.

sentences.zh: 父慶孫，申州團練判官，有詩名。

translations.literal: His father Qingsun was defense commissioner judge of Shen Prefecture and had a reputation for poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingsun was defense commissioner judge of Shen Prefecture and had a reputation for poetry.

sentences.zh: 常少好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Chang from youth loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chang loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐二年擢進士第，裁二十一，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Gan You of Han he was selected for the jinshi degree at only twenty-one and upon entering office became collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Gan You of Han he was selected for the jinshi degree at only twenty-one and upon entering office became collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，宰相範質奏充集賢校理，出為鄆州觀察支使，曆永興軍節度掌書記、伊陽令。

translations.literal: During Guangshun of Zhou, Chief Minister Fan Zhi memorialized to appoint him collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies. He went out to serve as administrative aide to the Yunzhou Observation Commissioner, and subsequently served as chief secretary under the Yongxing military commissioner and as magistrate of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun era of Zhou, Chief Minister Fan Zhi memorialized to appoint him collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies. He went out to serve as administrative aide to the Yunzhou Observation Commissioner and subsequently served as chief secretary under the Yongxing military commissioner and as magistrate of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年，詣闕進策，召試，復授猗氏令，遷蔡州防禦判官，復宰介休、魏縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he went to court to submit a policy memorial, was summoned for examination, and was again appointed magistrate of Yishi. He was transferred to defense commissioner judge of Cai Prefecture and again served as magistrate of Jiexiu and Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiande he went to court to submit a policy memorial, was summoned for examination, and was again appointed magistrate of Yishi. He was transferred to defense commissioner judge of Cai Prefecture and again served as magistrate of Jiexiu and Wei County.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，趙普為相，擢為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, when Zhao Pu was chief minister, he was promoted to Assistant Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao, when Zhao Pu was chief minister, he was promoted to Assistant Archivist.

sentences.zh: 時任此官，惟常與楊徽之、李若拙、趙鄰幾四人，皆有名於時。

translations.literal: At that time those holding this office were only Chang together with Yang Huizhi, Li Ruozhuo, and Zhao Linji—four men all famous in their day.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only Chang, together with Yang Huizhi, Li Ruozhuo, and Zhao Linji, held this office—four men all famous in their day.

sentences.zh: 常應舉時，著《四時成歲賦》萬餘言，又為《春蘭賦》，頗存興托。

translations.literal: When Chang took the examinations he composed 《Fu on the Four Seasons Completing the Year》, more than ten thousand characters, and also wrote 《Fu on Spring Orchids》, which preserved considerable allegorical intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang took the examinations he composed 《Fu on the Four Seasons Completing the Year》, more than ten thousand characters, and also wrote 《Fu on Spring Orchids》, which preserved considerable allegorical intent.

sentences.zh: 後為清河令。

translations.literal: Later he served as magistrate of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as magistrate of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died, aged forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子仲謀，字有開，雍熙中進士，有材幹，曆御史、東京留守推官、陝西轉運，至兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhongmou, styled Youkai, passed the jinshi in Yongxi. Capable and resourceful, he successively served as censor, judicial officer under the eastern capital garrison commander, transport commissioner for Shaanxi, reaching Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongmou, styled Youkai, passed the jinshi in Yongxi. Capable and resourceful, he successively served as censor, judicial officer under the eastern capital garrison commander, transport commissioner for Shaanxi, and rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 仲謀集其父所為文成二十卷。

translations.literal: Zhongmou collected his father's writings into twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmou collected his father's writings into twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 弟愉，周廣順中進士，與常齊名。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yu passed the jinshi during Guangshun of Zhou and was as famous as Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yu passed the jinshi during the Guangshun era of Zhou and was as famous as Chang.

sentences.zh: 宋準，字子平，開封雍丘人。

translations.literal: Song Zhun, styled Ziping, was a native of Yongqiu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhun, styled Ziping, came from Yongqiu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 祖彥升，庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yansheng was Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yansheng was Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 父鵬，秘書郎。

translations.literal: His father Peng was a secretary in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Peng was a secretary in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 準開寶中舉進士，翰林學士李皞知貢舉，擢準甲科。

translations.literal: Zhun passed the jinshi during Kaibao. Hanlin Academician Li Hao supervised the examinations and ranked Zhun in the top class.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun passed the jinshi during Kaibao. Hanlin Academician Li Hao supervised the examinations and ranked Zhun in the top class.

sentences.zh: 會貢士徐士廉擊登聞鼓，訴皞用情取舍非當。

translations.literal: When tribute scholar Xu Shilian struck the Denunciation Drum at court, accusing Hao of favoritism in selection.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute scholar Xu Shilian struck the Denunciation Drum at court, accusing Li Hao of favoritism in selection.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，召準覆試於便殿，見準形神偉茂，程試敏速，甚嘉之，以為宜首冠俊造，由是復擢準甲科，即授秘書省校書郎、直史館。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu was angered and summoned Zhun for a retest in the informal hall. Seeing Zhun's imposing presence and swift performance in the timed examination, he greatly admired him and judged that he should head the outstanding graduates. Thereupon Zhun was again ranked in the top class and immediately appointed collator in the Secretariat and assigned to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu was angered and summoned Zhun for a retest in the informal hall. Seeing Zhun's imposing presence and swift performance in the timed examination, he greatly admired him and judged that he should head the outstanding graduates. Thereupon Zhun was again ranked in the top class and immediately appointed collator in the Secretariat and assigned to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 八年，受詔修定諸道圖經。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he received an edict to revise and fix the gazetteers of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he received an edict to revise and fix the gazetteers of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 俄奉使契丹，復命稱旨。

translations.literal: Soon after he went on mission to the Khitan; on his return his report pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he went on mission to the Khitan, and on his return his report pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 明年，出知南平軍，會改軍為太平州，依前知州事，就加著作佐郎。

translations.literal: The next year he went out to administer Nanping Army. When the army was changed to Taiping Prefecture, he continued to administer prefectural affairs and was concurrently promoted to Assistant Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he went out to administer Nanping Army. When the army was changed to Taiping Prefecture, he continued to administer prefectural affairs and was concurrently promoted to Assistant Archivist.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，遷著作郎、通判梓州，轉左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to Archivist and administrative vice prefect of Zizhou, and became Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to Archivist and administrative vice prefect of Zizhou, and became Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，預修諸書。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he participated in compiling various books.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, he participated in compiling various books.

sentences.zh: 八年，同知貢舉，出為河北轉運使，歲餘，以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he jointly supervised the examinations, went out as transport commissioner of Hebei, and after a year was appointed drafter of edicts in his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he jointly supervised the examinations, went out as transport commissioner of Hebei, and after a year was appointed drafter of edicts in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，加主客員外郎，復預知貢舉，俄判大理寺。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he was additionally appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Reception, again jointly supervised the examinations, and soon judged the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was additionally appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Reception, again jointly supervised the examinations, and soon judged the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 四年，被病，遷金部郎中，罷知制誥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he fell ill, was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and relieved of duty as drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he fell ill, was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and relieved of duty as drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年卒，年五十二，賜錢百萬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong he died, aged fifty-two, and was granted a million cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong he died, aged fifty-two, and was granted a million cash.

sentences.zh: 準美風儀，善談論，辭采清麗，蒞官所至，皆有治聲。

translations.literal: Zhun had fine bearing, was skilled at discourse, and his diction was clear and elegant. Wherever he took office he had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun had fine bearing, was skilled at discourse, and his diction was clear and elegant. Wherever he took office he had a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 盧多遜之南流也，李穆坐同門生黜免，左右無敢言者。

translations.literal: When Lu Duoxun was exiled south, Li Mu was dismissed for being a fellow disciple; no one around the emperor dared speak on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Duoxun was exiled south, Li Mu was dismissed for being a fellow disciple, and no one around the emperor dared speak on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 準因奏事，盛言穆長者，有檢操，常惡多遜專恣，固非其黨也。

translations.literal: Zhun, while reporting on affairs, spoke at length that Mu was a man of exemplary character with self-restraint, had always hated Lu Duoxun's willfulness, and was certainly not of his faction.
translations.idiomatic: While reporting on affairs, Zhun spoke at length that Mu was a man of exemplary character with self-restraint, had always hated Lu Duoxun's willfulness, and was certainly not of his faction.

sentences.zh: 上寤，未幾，盡復穆舊官。

translations.literal: The emperor came to his senses, and before long fully restored Mu's former offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to his senses, and before long fully restored Mu's former offices.

sentences.zh: 時論以此稱之。

translations.literal: Public opinion praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年，錄其子大年試秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianxi his son Danian was recorded and tested as collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianxi his son Danian was recorded and tested as collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 準從弟可觀，金部郎中。

translations.literal: Zhun's cousin second younger brother Keguan was Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun's cousin Keguan was Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 族子郊、祁，並天聖二年進士甲科，別有傳。

translations.literal: His clansmen sons Jiao and Qi both passed the top jinshi class in the second year of Tiansheng; they have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His clansmen Jiao and Qi both passed the top jinshi class in the second year of Tiansheng; they have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 柳開，字仲塗，大名人。

translations.literal: Liu Kai, styled Zhongtu, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kai, styled Zhongtu, came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 父承翰，乾德初監察御史。

translations.literal: His father Chenghan, at the beginning of Qian De served as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chenghan, at the beginning of the Qian De era, served as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 開幼穎異，有膽勇。

translations.literal: Kai from childhood was exceptionally bright and had courage.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Kai was exceptionally bright and had courage.

sentences.zh: 周顯德末，侍父任南樂，夜與家人立庭中，有盜入室，眾恐不敢動，開裁十三，亟取劍逐之，盜逾垣出，開揮刃斷二足指。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiande of Zhou, while attending his father on assignment at Nanle, one night he stood in the courtyard with his family. A thief entered the house; everyone was afraid and dared not move. Kai was only thirteen; he quickly took a sword and pursued. The thief climbed over the wall to escape; Kai swung his blade and severed two toes.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiande era of Zhou, while attending his father on assignment at Nanle, one night he stood in the courtyard with his family. A thief entered the house; everyone was afraid and dared not move. Kai was only thirteen. He quickly took a sword and pursued. The thief climbed over the wall to escape, and Kai swung his blade and severed two toes.

sentences.zh: 既就學，喜討論經義。

translations.literal: Once he began his studies he delighted in discussing the meaning of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Once he began his studies he delighted in discussing the meaning of the classics.

sentences.zh: 五代文格淺弱，慕韓愈、柳宗元為文，因名肩愈，字紹先。

translations.literal: The literary style of the Five Dynasties was shallow and weak; he admired Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan in writing, and therefore took the name Jingyou, styled Shaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: The literary style of the Five Dynasties was shallow and weak. He admired Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan in writing and therefore took the name Jingyou, styled Shaoxian.

sentences.zh: 既而改名字，以為能開聖道之塗也。

translations.literal: Later he changed his given name and style, believing he could open the path of the sage Way.
translations.idiomatic: Later he changed his given name and style, believing he could open the path of the sage Way.

sentences.zh: 著書自號東郊野夫，又號補亡先生，作二傳以見意。

translations.literal: In his writings he styled himself Eastern Suburb Recluse and also called himself Master Who Makes Up for Loss; he wrote two biographies to express his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In his writings he styled himself Eastern Suburb Recluse and also called himself Master Who Makes Up for Loss. He wrote two biographies to express his meaning.

sentences.zh: 尚氣自任，不顧小節，所交皆一時豪雋。

translations.literal: He valued bold spirit and trusted himself, heedless of minor proprieties; those he befriended were all leading men of talent of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He valued bold spirit and trusted himself, heedless of minor proprieties, and those he befriended were all leading men of talent of the age.

sentences.zh: 範杲好古學，尤重開文，世稱為「柳、範」。

translations.literal: Fan Gao loved ancient learning and especially valued Kai's writing; the world called them "Liu and Fan."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Gao loved ancient learning and especially valued Kai's writing. The world called them "Liu and Fan."

sentences.zh: 王祐知大名，開以文贄大蒙賞激。

translations.literal: When Wang You was prefect of Daming, Kai presented literary gifts and received great encouragement and praise.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang You was prefect of Daming, Kai presented literary gifts and received great encouragement and praise.

sentences.zh: 楊昭儉、盧多遜並加延獎。

translations.literal: Yang Zhaojian and Lu Duoxun both extended praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhaojian and Lu Duoxun both extended praise and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年舉進士，補宋州司寇參軍，以治獄稱職，遷本州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Si Kou Canjun in Songzhou, was considered competent in judging legal cases, and was promoted to Luchshi Canjun in the same prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Si Kou Canjun in Songzhou. He earned a reputation for competence in judging legal cases and was promoted to Luchshi Canjun in the same prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，擢右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: During the Taiping Xingguo era, he was promoted to Right Zanshan Dafu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era he was promoted to Right Zanshan Dafu.

sentences.zh: 會征太原，督楚、泗八州運糧。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Taiyuan was launched, he supervised grain transport from eight prefectures of Chu and Si.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Taiyuan was launched, he supervised grain transport from the eight prefectures of Chu and Si.

sentences.zh: 選知常州，遷殿中丞，徙潤州，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Selected to serve as prefect of Changzhou; promoted to Dianzhong Cheng; transferred to Runzhou; appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected to serve as prefect of Changzhou, promoted to Dianzhong Cheng, transferred to Runzhou, and appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 召還，知貝州，轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Recalled to court; appointed prefect of Beizhou; transferred to Palace Attendant Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court, appointed prefect of Beizhou, and transferred to Palace Attendant Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，坐與監軍忿爭，貶上蔡令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, because of a heated quarrel with the military inspector, he was demoted to Magistrate of Shangcai.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, after a heated quarrel with the military inspector, he was demoted to magistrate of Shangcai.

sentences.zh: 會大舉北征，開部送軍糧，將至涿州，有契丹酋長領萬騎與米信戰，相持不解，俄遣使紿言求降，開謂信曰：「兵法云：『無約而請和，謀也。』

translations.literal: When a major northern campaign was launched, Kai escorted military grain supplies. As they approached Zhuozhou, a Khitan chieftain leading ten thousand horsemen fought with Mi Xin in a stalemate. Soon emissaries were sent falsely claiming they sought surrender. Kai said to Xin: "The Art of War says: 'To seek peace without prior agreement is a stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: When a major northern campaign was launched, Kai escorted military grain supplies. As they neared Zhuozhou, a Khitan chieftain leading ten thousand horsemen fought Mi Xin to a standstill. Soon emissaries arrived with a false offer of surrender. Kai said to Xin, "The Art of War says: 'To seek peace without prior agreement is a stratagem.

sentences.zh: 彼將有謀，急攻之必勝。」

translations.literal: They are plotting; if we attack swiftly we are sure to win."
translations.idiomatic: They are plotting. Attack at once and you are sure to win."

sentences.zh: 信遲疑不決。

translations.literal: Xin hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Xin hesitated and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 逾二日，賊復引兵挑戰，後偵知果以矢盡，俟取於幽州也。

translations.literal: After more than two days, the enemy again led troops out to challenge battle. Later reconnaissance revealed they had indeed exhausted their arrows and were waiting to fetch more from Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: More than two days later the enemy again led troops out to offer battle. Later reconnaissance revealed they had indeed run out of arrows and were waiting for fresh supplies from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，詣闕上書，願從邊軍效死，太宗憐之，復授殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he went to the capital and submitted a memorial, offering to follow the frontier armies and die in service. Emperor Taizong took pity on him and restored him as Palace Attendant Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he went to the capital and submitted a memorial offering to follow the frontier armies and die in service. Emperor Taizong took pity on him and restored him as Palace Attendant Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，使河北，因抗疏曰：「臣受非常恩，未有以報，年裁四十，膽力方壯。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, on mission to Hebei, he submitted a direct memorial saying: "I have received extraordinary grace and have no means to repay it. I am barely forty, and my courage and strength are at their peak.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi, while on mission to Hebei, he submitted a direct memorial saying, "I have received extraordinary grace and have no way to repay it. I am barely forty, and my courage and strength are at their peak.

sentences.zh: 今契丹未滅，願陛下賜臣步騎數千，任以河北用兵之地，必能出生入死，為陛下復幽、薊，雖身沒戰場，臣之願也。」

translations.literal: The Khitan are not yet destroyed. I beg Your Majesty to grant me several thousand infantry and cavalry and assign me a field of operations in Hebei. I can surely risk life and limb to recover You and Ji for Your Majesty—even if I perish on the battlefield, that is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan are not yet destroyed. I beg Your Majesty to grant me several thousand infantry and cavalry and assign me a field of operations in Hebei. I can surely risk life and limb to recover You and Ji for Your Majesty—even if I fall on the battlefield, that is my wish."

sentences.zh: 上以五代戰爭以來，自節鎮至刺史皆用武臣，多不曉政事，人受其弊。

translations.literal: The Emperor, knowing that since the wars of the Five Dynasties, from military commissioners down to prefects all had been military men who often did not understand civil administration, and the people suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew that since the wars of the Five Dynasties, from military commissioners down to prefects, posts had gone to military men who often did not understand civil administration, and the people had suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 欲兼用文士，乃以侍御史鄭宣、戶部員外郎趙載、司門員外郎劉墀並為如京使，左拾遺劉慶為西京作坊使，開為崇儀使、知寧邊軍。

translations.literal: Wishing also to employ literary men, he therefore appointed Supervising Censor Zheng Xuan, Vice Commissioner of Revenue Zhao Zai, and Vice Director of the Gate Office Liu Chi all as Rujing Envoys; Left Remonstrance Official Liu Qing as West Capital Workshop Commissioner; and Kai as Chongyi Commissioner and commander of the Ningbian Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing also to employ literary men, he appointed Supervising Censor Zheng Xuan, Vice Commissioner of Revenue Zhao Zai, and Vice Director of the Gate Office Liu Chi all as Rujing Envoys; Left Remonstrance Official Liu Qing as West Capital Workshop Commissioner; and Kai as Chongyi Commissioner and commander of the Ningbian Army.

sentences.zh: 徙全州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 全西溪洞有粟氏，聚族五百餘人，常鈔劫民口糧畜，開為作衣帶巾帽，選牙吏勇辯者得三輩，使入，諭之曰：「爾能歸我，即有厚賞，給田為屋處之；

translations.literal: In West Creek Cave of Quanzhou there was the Su clan, a group of more than five hundred who regularly robbed the people of their grain and livestock. Kai had clothing, belts, caps, and hats made for them, selected three groups of brave and eloquent clerks, and sent them in to instruct them, saying: "If you submit to me, you will receive rich rewards—fields and houses will be given for your settlement;
translations.idiomatic: In West Creek Cave of Quanzhou lived the Su clan, more than five hundred strong, who regularly robbed the people of grain and livestock. Kai had clothing, belts, caps, and hats made for them, chose three groups of brave and eloquent clerks, and sent them in with this message: "If you submit to me, you will receive rich rewards—we will give you fields and houses to settle in;

sentences.zh: 不然，發兵深入，滅爾類矣。」

translations.literal: otherwise I will send troops deep into your territory and exterminate your kind."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I will send troops deep into your territory and wipe out your entire clan."

sentences.zh: 粟氏懼，留二吏為質，率其酋四人與一吏偕來。

translations.literal: The Su clan were afraid; they left two clerks as hostages and led four of their chiefs together with one clerk to come.
translations.idiomatic: The Su clan were afraid. They left two clerks as hostages and led four of their chiefs together with one clerk to come in person.

sentences.zh: 開厚其犒賜，吏民爭以鼓吹飲之。

translations.literal: Kai richly rewarded them with gifts and feasts; officials and commoners vied to entertain them with drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Kai richly rewarded them with gifts and feasts, and officials and commoners vied to entertain them with drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 居數日遣還，如期攜老幼悉至。

translations.literal: After several days he sent them back; on schedule they brought all their old and young.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he sent them back, and on schedule they returned with all their old and young.

sentences.zh: 開即賦其居業，作《時鑒》一篇，刻石戒之。

translations.literal: Kai then assessed their dwellings and property, composed a piece titled 《Season Mirror》, and had it carved in stone as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Kai then assessed their dwellings and property, composed 《Season Mirror》, and had it carved in stone as a warning.

sentences.zh: 遣其酋入朝，授本州上佐。

translations.literal: He sent their chiefs to court and had them appointed senior aides of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He sent their chiefs to court and had them appointed senior aides of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賜開錢三十萬。

translations.literal: Kai was granted three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was granted three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，移知桂州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was transferred to serve as prefect of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chunhua he was transferred to serve as prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，開在全州，有卒訟開，開即杖背黥麵送闕下。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Kai was at Quanzhou, a soldier sued him. Kai immediately had him beaten on the back, tattooed on the face, and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Kai was at Quanzhou, a soldier brought suit against him. Kai immediately had him beaten on the back, tattooed on the face, and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 有司言卒罪不及徒，召開下御史獄劾係，削二官，黜為復州團練副使，移滁州。

translations.literal: The authorities said the soldier's offense did not warrant banishment. Kai was summoned, imprisoned in the censor's jail for investigation, stripped of two ranks, demoted to Deputy Military Training Commissioner of Fuzhou, and transferred to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities ruled that the soldier's offense did not warrant banishment. Kai was summoned, imprisoned in the censor's jail for investigation, stripped of two ranks, demoted to Deputy Military Training Commissioner of Fuzhou, and transferred to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 復舊官，知環州。

translations.literal: His former rank was restored; he was appointed prefect of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His former rank was restored and he was appointed prefect of Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，移邠州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 時調民輦送趨環慶，己再運，民皆蕩析產業，轉運使復督後運，民數千人入州署號訴。

translations.literal: At the time the people were levied to haul supplies hastily to Huan and Qing. They had already made two transport runs and all had exhausted their property. The transport commissioner again pressed for further runs; several thousand people entered the prefectural office wailing in protest.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the people were levied to haul supplies in haste to Huan and Qing. They had already made two transport runs and exhausted their property, yet the transport commissioner again pressed for further runs. Several thousand people entered the prefectural office wailing in protest.

sentences.zh: 開貽書轉運使曰：「開近離環州，知芻糧之數不增，大兵可支四年，今蠶農方作，再運半發，老幼疲弊，畜乘困竭，奈何又苦之？

translations.literal: Kai sent a letter to the transport commissioner saying: "Kai has recently left Huanzhou and knows the amount of forage has not increased—the main army can be supplied for four years. Now sericulture and farming are underway; the second transport run is only half dispatched. The old and young are worn out, draft animals exhausted—why afflict them further?
translations.idiomatic: Kai sent a letter to the transport commissioner saying, "I have recently left Huanzhou and know the amount of forage has not increased—the main army can be supplied for four years. Sericulture and farming are now underway, and the second transport run is only half complete. The old and young are worn out and draft animals exhausted—why afflict them further?

sentences.zh: 不罷，開即馳詣闕下，白於上前矣。」

translations.literal: If it is not halted, Kai will ride post-haste to the capital and report it directly before the throne."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not halt it, I will ride post-haste to the capital and report it directly before the throne."

sentences.zh: 卒罷之。

translations.literal: In the end it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the order was stopped.

sentences.zh: 又知曹、邢二州。

translations.literal: He also served as prefect of Cao and Xing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as prefect of Cao and Xing prefectures.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加如京使，歸朝，命知代州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, he was added the title Rujing Envoy; recalled to court; appointed prefect of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, Kai was given the additional title of Rujing Envoy, recalled to court, and appointed prefect of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 上言曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 國家創業將四十年，陛下紹二聖之祚，精求至治。

translations.literal: The state has been established for nearly forty years; Your Majesty has inherited the fortune of two sages and diligently seeks perfect governance.
translations.idiomatic: The state has been established for nearly forty years. Your Majesty has inherited the fortune of two sages and diligently seeks perfect governance.

sentences.zh: 若守舊規，斯未盡善。

translations.literal: If we merely abide by old rules, we have not yet attained what is best.
translations.idiomatic: If we merely abide by old rules, we have not yet attained what is best.

sentences.zh: 能立新法，乃顯神機。

translations.literal: Only by establishing new methods can divine ingenuity be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Only by establishing new methods can divine ingenuity be displayed.

sentences.zh: 臣以益州稍靜，望陛下選賢能以鎮之，必須望重有威，即群小畏服。

translations.literal: I consider that Yizhou has grown somewhat calm. I hope Your Majesty will select a worthy man of ability to guard it—one whose prestige and authority are weighty, so that petty men will fear and submit.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that Yizhou has grown somewhat calm. I hope Your Majesty will select a worthy man of ability to guard it—one whose prestige and authority are weighty, so that petty men will fear and submit.

sentences.zh: 又西鄙今雖歸明，他日未可必保，苟有翻覆，須得人制禦，若以契丹比議，為患更深。

translations.literal: Further, though the western borderlands now submit to enlightenment, in future they cannot be guaranteed; should there be reversal, men must be found to check them. If compared with the Khitan threat, the harm is even deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Further, though the western borderlands now submit to the court, they cannot be guaranteed in future. Should they turn, men must be found to check them—and compared with the Khitan threat, the harm would be even deeper.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 契丹則君臣久定，蕃、漢久分，縱萌南顧之心，亦須自有思慮。

translations.literal: With the Khitan, ruler and ministers have long been settled, tribal and Han long separated—even if they harbor thoughts of turning south, they must still deliberate for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: With the Khitan, ruler and ministers have long been settled and tribal and Han long separated. Even if they harbor thoughts of turning south, they must still weigh the matter for themselves.

sentences.zh: 西鄙積恨未泯，貪心不悛，其下猖狂，競謀凶惡，侵漁未必知足，姑息未能感恩，望常預備之。

translations.literal: In the western borderlands accumulated hatred is not yet extinguished, greed is not reformed; those below are reckless, competing in wicked plots. Plundering may never know satiety, indulgence cannot win gratitude—I hope constant preparation will be made.
translations.idiomatic: In the western borderlands accumulated hatred is not yet extinguished and greed is not reformed. Those below are reckless and compete in wicked plots. Plunder may never know satiety, and indulgence cannot win gratitude. I hope constant preparation will be made.

sentences.zh: 以良將守其要害，以厚賜足其貪婪，以撫慰來其情，以寬假息其念。

translations.literal: Place good generals to guard critical points; use lavish gifts to satisfy their greed; use soothing words to win their hearts; use leniency to quiet their thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Place good generals to guard critical points; use lavish gifts to satisfy their greed; use soothing words to win their hearts; use leniency to quiet their restless thoughts.

sentences.zh: 多命人使西入甘、涼，厚結其心，為我聲援，如有動靜，使其掩襲，令彼有後顧之憂，乃可制其輕動。

translations.literal: Frequently send envoys west into Gan and Liang to bind their hearts closely, making them our vocal allies. If there is any movement, have them launch surprise attacks so the enemy will have worries behind them—only then can their rash actions be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Frequently send envoys west into Gan and Liang to bind their hearts closely and make them our allies in word and deed. If there is any movement, have them launch surprise attacks so the enemy will have worries behind them—only then can their rash actions be restrained.

sentences.zh: 今甲兵雖眾，不及太祖之時人人練習，謀臣猛將則又縣殊，是以比年西北屢遭侵擾，養育則月費甚廣，征戰則軍捷未聞。

translations.literal: Now though armored troops are numerous, they fall short of the Taizu era when every man practiced; strategists and fierce generals are even more scarce. Therefore in recent years the northwest has suffered repeated incursions—rearing troops costs vast monthly expense, yet in campaigns no military victories are heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Now though armored troops are numerous, they fall short of the Taizu era when every man drilled. Strategists and fierce generals are even scarcer. Therefore in recent years the northwest has suffered repeated incursions—rearing troops costs vast monthly expense, yet in campaigns no victories are heard of.

sentences.zh: 誠願訓練禁戢，使如往日行伍必求於勇敢，指顧無縱於後先，失律者悉誅，獲功者必賞。

translations.literal: I earnestly wish training and discipline enforced, so that as in former days ranks seek the brave, commands allow no lagging fore or aft, all who break discipline be punished, and all who gain merit be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly wish training and discipline enforced, so that as in former days ranks seek the brave, commands allow no lagging fore or aft, all who break discipline be punished, and all who gain merit be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 偏裨主將，不威嚴者去之。

translations.literal: Assistant commanders and chief generals who lack awesomeness—remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant commanders and chief generals who lack awesomeness should be removed.

sentences.zh: 聽斷之暇，親臨殿庭，更召貔虎，使其擊刺馳驟，以彰神武之盛。

translations.literal: In leisure from judging affairs, personally visit the palace yard, summon the brave warriors again, and have them strike, thrust, gallop, and charge—to display the splendor of divine martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure from judging affairs, personally visit the palace yard, summon the brave warriors again, and have them strike, thrust, gallop, and charge—to display the splendor of divine martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 臣又以宰相、樞密，朝廷大臣，委之必無疑，用之必至當。

translations.literal: I further hold that the Chancellor and Military Affairs Commissioner, as great ministers of court, if entrusted surely inspire no doubt, if used surely reach full appropriateness.
translations.idiomatic: I further hold that the Chancellor and Military Affairs Commissioner, as great ministers of court, if entrusted inspire no doubt and if used reach full appropriateness.

sentences.zh: 銓總僚屬，評品職官，內則主管百司，外則分治四海。

translations.literal: They oversee and gather subordinates, assess and rank officials—within they manage the hundred offices, without they divide governance of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: They oversee and gather subordinates and assess and rank officials—within they manage the hundred offices, without they divide governance of the four seas.

sentences.zh: 今京朝官則別置審官，供奉、殿直則別立三班，刑部不令詳斷，別立審刑，宣徽一司全同散地。

translations.literal: Now for capital officials a separate Bureau of Review is established; for inner-palace attendants and palace direct attendants a separate Three Ranks is set up; the Ministry of Justice is not allowed to conduct detailed judgments—a separate Bureau of Reviewed Sentences is established; the Xuanhui Department as a whole is like idle territory.
translations.idiomatic: Now for capital officials a separate Bureau of Review is established; for inner-palace attendants and palace direct attendants a separate Three Ranks is set up; the Ministry of Justice is not allowed to conduct detailed judgments and a separate Bureau of Reviewed Sentences is established; the Xuanhui Department as a whole is like idle territory.

sentences.zh: 大臣不獲親信，小臣乃謂至公。

translations.literal: Great ministers cannot gain intimate trust, while petty officials are deemed perfectly impartial.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers cannot gain intimate trust, while petty officials are deemed perfectly impartial.

sentences.zh: 至如銀台一司，舊屬樞密，近年改製，職掌甚多，加倍置人，事則依舊，別無利害，虛有變更。

translations.literal: As for the Yintai Office—it formerly belonged to Military Affairs; in recent years its system was changed: duties are greatly multiplied, personnel doubled, yet the work remains as before—no benefit or harm, only empty change.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Yintai Office—it formerly belonged to Military Affairs; in recent years its system was changed, duties greatly multiplied, and personnel doubled, yet the work remains as before—no benefit or harm, only empty change.

sentences.zh: 臣欲望停審官、三班，復委中書、樞密、宣徽院，銀台司復歸樞密，審刑院復歸刑部，去其繁細，省其頭目。

translations.literal: I wish to abolish the Bureau of Review and Three Ranks, restore authority to the Secretariat, Military Affairs, and Xuanhui Court; return the Yintai Office to Military Affairs and the Bureau of Reviewed Sentences to the Ministry of Justice—cut away the excessive detail, reduce the ranks of officials.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to abolish the Bureau of Review and Three Ranks, restore authority to the Secretariat, Military Affairs, and Xuanhui Court, return the Yintai Office to Military Affairs and the Bureau of Reviewed Sentences to the Ministry of Justice, and cut away excessive detail and reduce the ranks of officials.

sentences.zh: 又京府大都，萬方軌則，望仍舊貫，選委親賢。

translations.literal: Further, the capital prefectures are great metropolises, models for all regions—I hope the old practice may be restored and trusted kinsmen and worthies selected and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Further, the capital prefectures are great metropolises and models for all regions. I hope the old practice may be restored and trusted kinsmen and worthies selected and appointed.

sentences.zh: 今皇族宗子悉多成長，但令優逸，無以試材，宜委之外藩，擇文武忠直之士，為左右讚弼之任。

translations.literal: Now imperial clan members and royal sons are mostly grown, yet given only ease and comfort with no means to test their talents. They should be assigned to outer prefectures, with loyal and upright men of civil and military talent chosen as their left and right aides and advisors.
translations.idiomatic: Now imperial clan members and royal sons are mostly grown, yet given only ease and comfort with no means to test their talents. They should be assigned to outer prefectures, with loyal and upright men of civil and military talent chosen as their left and right aides and advisors.

sentences.zh: 又天下州縣官吏不均，或冗長至多，或歲年久闕。

translations.literal: Further, officials in prefectures and counties throughout the realm are unevenly distributed—some places have excessive redundancy, some have posts vacant for years.
translations.idiomatic: Further, officials in prefectures and counties throughout the realm are unevenly distributed—some places have excessive redundancy, others have posts vacant for years.

sentences.zh: 欲望縣四千戶已上選朝官知，三千戶已上選京官知。

translations.literal: I wish that for counties with four thousand households and above, capital officials be selected as magistrates; for three thousand households and above, capital-service officials be selected.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that for counties with four thousand households and above, capital officials be selected as magistrates, and for three thousand households and above, capital-service officials be selected.

sentences.zh: 省去主簿，令縣尉兼領其事。

translations.literal: Abolish the registrar and have the county sheriff concurrently perform those duties.
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the registrar and have the county sheriff concurrently perform those duties.

sentences.zh: 自餘通判、監軍、巡檢、監臨使臣並酌量省減，免虛費於利祿，仍均濟於職官。

translations.literal: All remaining military supervisors, patrol inspectors, and supervising envoys should be proportionally reduced, eliminating wasteful salary expenditure while balancing official posts.
translations.idiomatic: All remaining military supervisors, patrol inspectors, and supervising envoys should be proportionally reduced, eliminating wasteful salary expenditure while balancing official posts.

sentences.zh: 又人情貪競，時態輕浮，雖骨肉之至親，臨勢利而多變。

translations.literal: Further, human nature is grasping and competitive, the temper of the times frivolous—even the closest of kin, when facing power and profit, often change.
translations.idiomatic: Further, human nature is grasping and competitive and the temper of the times frivolous—even the closest of kin, when power and profit are at stake, often change.

sentences.zh: 同僚之內，多或不和，伺隙則致於傾危，患難則全無相救，仁義之風蕩然不復。

translations.literal: Among colleagues many are not harmonious—watching for openings they bring each other to ruin; in hardship they offer no rescue—the wind of benevolence and righteousness has utterly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Among colleagues many are not harmonious—watching for openings they bring each other to ruin, and in hardship they offer no rescue. The wind of benevolence and righteousness has utterly vanished.

sentences.zh: 欲望有頒告諭，各使改更，庶厚化原，永敦政本。

translations.literal: I hope an edict may be issued to instruct all to reform, that the source of deep transformation may be cultivated and the foundation of governance perpetually upheld.
translations.idiomatic: I hope an edict may be issued instructing all to reform, that the source of deep transformation may be cultivated and the foundation of governance perpetually upheld.

sentences.zh: 恭惟太祖神武，太宗聖文，光掩百王，威加萬國，無賢不用，無事不知。

translations.literal: Reverently considering Taizu divine in martial prowess, Taizong sage in literary accomplishment—splendor eclipsing the hundred kings, might extending over the myriad states—no worthy left unused, nothing of affairs unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently considering Taizu divine in martial prowess and Taizong sage in literary accomplishment—splendor eclipsing the hundred kings, might extending over the myriad states—no worthy left unused and nothing of affairs unknown.

sentences.zh: 望陛下開豁聖懷，如天如海，可斷即斷，合行即行，愛惜忠直之臣，體察奸諛之黨。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will open wide Your sage mind, vast as heaven and sea—decide when decision is needed, act when action is fitting; cherish loyal and straight officers, discern the factions of flattery and sycophancy.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will open wide Your sage mind, vast as heaven and sea—decide when decision is needed, act when action is fitting, cherish loyal and straight officers, and discern the factions of flattery and sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 臣久塵著位，寢荷恩寵，辭狂理拙，唯聖明恕之！

translations.literal: Your subject long tarnishes a prominent post, ever burdened by grace and favor—my words are wild and reasoning crude; only may the sage brilliance forgive!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject long tarnishes a prominent post, ever burdened by grace and favor. My words are wild and my reasoning crude—only may the sage brilliance forgive!

sentences.zh: 開至州，葺城壘戰具，諸將多沮議不協。

translations.literal: When Kai reached the prefecture, he repaired walls, ramparts, and battle equipment. Many generals discouraged the plan and were not in accord.
translations.idiomatic: When Kai reached the prefecture, he repaired walls, ramparts, and battle equipment, but many generals discouraged the plan and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 開謂其從子曰：「吾觀昂宿有光，雲多從北來犯境上，寇將至矣。

translations.literal: Kai said to his attendant son: "I observe the Horn constellation has light; clouds mostly come from the north invading our borders—the enemy is about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Kai said to his attendant son, "I observe the Horn constellation has light and clouds mostly come from the north across our borders—the enemy is about to arrive.

sentences.zh: 吾聞師克在和，今諸將怨我，一旦寇至，必危我矣。」

translations.literal: I have heard an army conquers through harmony. Now the generals resent me; once the enemy comes, they will surely endanger me."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that an army conquers through harmony. Now the generals resent me—once the enemy comes, they will surely endanger me."

sentences.zh: 即求換郡，徙忻州刺史。

translations.literal: He immediately requested transfer to another prefecture and was moved to Prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately requested transfer to another prefecture and was moved to prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及契丹犯邊，開上書，又請車駕觀兵河朔。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the border, Kai submitted a memorial again requesting the imperial carriage observe troops in the Hebei region.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded the border, Kai submitted a memorial again requesting that the imperial carriage observe troops in the Hebei region.

sentences.zh: 四年，徙滄州，道病首瘍卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Cangzhou; on the road he died of a head sore at age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Cangzhou; on the road he died of a head sore at age fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 錄其子涉為三班奉職。

translations.literal: His son She was enrolled as a Three-Ranks Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son She was enrolled as a Three-Ranks Attendant.

sentences.zh: 開善射，喜弈棋。

translations.literal: Kai was skilled at archery and fond of weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was skilled at archery and fond of weiqi.

sentences.zh: 有集十五卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in fifteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in fifteen juan.

sentences.zh: 作《家戒》千餘言，刻石以訓諸子。

translations.literal: He wrote 《Family Admonitions》 of more than a thousand words and had it carved in stone to instruct his sons.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote 《Family Admonitions》, more than a thousand words long, and had it carved in stone to instruct his sons.

sentences.zh: 性倜儻重義。

translations.literal: By nature he was free-spirited and valued righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was free-spirited and valued righteousness.

sentences.zh: 在大名，嘗過酒肆飲，有士人在旁，辭貌稍異，開詢其名，則至自京師，以貧不克葬其親，聞王祐篤義，將丐之。

translations.literal: At Daming, once passing a wine shop to drink, there was a scholar at his side whose speech and appearance were somewhat unusual. Kai asked his name and learned he had come from the capital—too poor to bury his parents, he had heard Wang You was deeply righteous and intended to beg him for help.
translations.idiomatic: At Daming, once passing a wine shop to drink, he noticed a scholar at his side whose speech and appearance were somewhat unusual. Kai asked his name and learned he had come from the capital—too poor to bury his parents, he had heard Wang You was deeply righteous and intended to beg him for help.

sentences.zh: 問所費，曰：「二十萬足矣。」

translations.literal: Asked the cost, he said: "Two hundred thousand would suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Asked the cost, he said, "Two hundred thousand would suffice."

sentences.zh: 開即罄所有，得白金百餘兩，益錢數萬遣之。

translations.literal: Kai immediately emptied all he had—obtaining more than a hundred taels of white silver and adding several ten-thousands in cash, he sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Kai immediately emptied all he had—gathering more than a hundred taels of white silver and adding several ten-thousands in cash, he sent the man on his way.

sentences.zh: 開兄肩吾，至御史。

translations.literal: Kai's elder brother Jianwu reached Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's elder brother Jianwu rose to the rank of censor.

sentences.zh: 肩吾三子，湜、灝、沆並進士第，灝秘書丞。

translations.literal: Jianwu's three sons Shi, Hao, and Hang all passed the jinshi examination; Hao was Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu's three sons Shi, Hao, and Hang all passed the jinshi examination; Hao served as Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 夏侯嘉，正字會之，江陵人，少有俊才。

translations.literal: Xia Houjiazheng, styled Huizhi, was a native of Jiangling and in youth possessed outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Houjiazheng, styled Huizhi, was a native of Jiangling and in youth possessed outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中舉進士，曆官至著作佐郎。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to Assistant Author.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to Assistant Author.

sentences.zh: 使於巴陵，為《洞庭賦》曰：

translations.literal: On mission to Baling, he wrote 《Rhapsody on Dongting》 saying:
translations.idiomatic: On mission to Baling, he wrote 《Rhapsody on Dongting》, which begins:

sentences.zh: 楚之南有水曰洞庭，環帶五郡，淼不知其幾百里。

translations.literal: South of Chu is a body of water called Dongting, encircling five commanderies, vast and boundless for who knows how many hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: South of Chu lies a body of water called Dongting, girdling five commanderies in a vast expanse whose breadth no man can reckon in hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 臣乙酉夏使嶽陽，抵湖上，思構賦。

translations.literal: Your subject, in the yiwei year summer on mission to Yueyang, arrived at the lake's shore and thought to compose a rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, in the summer of the yiwei year on mission to Yueyang, came to the lake's shore and resolved to compose a rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 明日披襟而觀之，則翼然動，促然跂，慄然駭，愕然眙。

translations.literal: The next day, baring my breast to gaze upon it—the waters seemed to flutter like wings, surge upward on tiptoe, shiver in dread, startle in awe.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, baring my breast to gaze upon it, I saw the waters flutter as though winged, surge upward on tiptoe, shiver in dread, and startle me to wide-eyed awe.

sentences.zh: 怳若駕春雲而軾霓，浩若浮汗漫而朝躋。

translations.literal: Dizzied as though driving spring clouds while striding a rainbow; vast as floating on boundless heavens while climbing toward dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I grew dizzy as though driving spring clouds and striding a rainbow, vast as floating on the boundless heavens while climbing toward dawn.

sentences.zh: 退若據泰山之安，進若履千仞之危。

translations.literal: In retreat like standing on the sureness of Mount Tai; in advance like treading the peril of a thousand-ren cliff.
translations.idiomatic: In retreat it seemed as secure as standing on Mount Tai; in advance as perilous as treading a cliff a thousand ren high.

sentences.zh: 懵若無識，智若通微。

translations.literal: Dazed as if without consciousness; awakened as if penetrating the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: I was dazed as if without consciousness, then awakened as if penetrating the subtle.

sentences.zh: 跛若不倚，蹌若將馳。

translations.literal: Limping as if without support; striding as if about to gallop.
translations.idiomatic: It lurched as if without support, then strode as if about to gallop.

sentences.zh: 耳不及掩，目不暇逃，情悸心嬉。

translations.literal: Ears could not cover fast enough; eyes could not flee in time—the heart trembles yet rejoices.
translations.idiomatic: My ears could not cover fast enough, my eyes could not flee in time—my heart trembled even as it rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 二三日而後，神始宅，氣始正，若此不敢以賦為事者二年，然眷眷不已。

translations.literal: Two or three days afterward, the spirit at last settled, the breath at last righted. Thus for two years I dared not make the rhapsody my task—yet longing never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Two or three days passed before my spirit at last settled and my breath at last righted. For two years after that I dared not take up the rhapsody as my task—yet longing never ceased.

sentences.zh: 一日登崇丘，望大澤，有雲卒兮興，兮止。

translations.literal: One day ascending a lofty hill, gazing upon the great marsh—clouds suddenly rose—and suddenly halted.
translations.idiomatic: One day I ascended a lofty hill and gazed upon the great marsh—clouds suddenly rose, then suddenly halted.

sentences.zh: 興止未霽，急若有遇。

translations.literal: Before rise and halt had cleared, urgency as though something were encountered.
translations.idiomatic: Before rise and halt had cleared, urgency seized me as though I had met with something.

sentences.zh: 由是漬陽輝，沐芳澤，睹一異人於岩之際，霞為裾，雲為袂，冰膚雪肌，金玦玉佩，浮丘、羨門，斯實其對。

translations.literal: Thereby bathed in solar radiance, rinsed in fragrant dew, I beheld a strange being at the cliff's verge—rainbow for skirt, cloud for sleeve, flesh of ice, limbs of snow, golden ring and jade pendants; Fuqiu and Xianmen—such were truly his match.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby bathed in solar radiance and rinsed in fragrant dew, I beheld a strange being at the cliff's verge—rainbow for skirt, cloud for sleeve, flesh of ice and limbs of snow, golden ring and jade pendants. Fuqiu and Xianmen were truly his match.

sentences.zh: 因言曰：「若非好辭者耶？」

translations.literal: Then he spoke, saying: "Are you not one who loves fine composition?"
translations.idiomatic: Then he spoke, saying, "Are you not one who loves fine composition?"

sentences.zh: 臣曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The minister said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The minister said, "It is so."

sentences.zh: 「然則若智有所不通，識有所不窮，用不通不窮而循乎無端之紀，若得無殆乎？」

translations.literal: Then if your wisdom has what it cannot penetrate and your understanding what it cannot exhaust, and you apply what is unpenetrating and inexhaustible to follow a principle without beginning—will you not come to harm?"
translations.idiomatic: Then if your wisdom has blind spots and your understanding its limits, and you apply what is limited and incomplete to follow an endless principle—will you not come to harm?"

sentences.zh: 臣又曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The minister again said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The minister again said, "It is so."

sentences.zh: 「然誌極則物應，思精則道來，嘉若之勤無嘩談，吾為若稱云：『太極之生，曰地曰天。

translations.literal: Yet when purpose reaches its utmost, things respond; when thought is refined, the Way arrives. I praise your diligent avoidance of idle talk, and will compose a hymn for you, saying: 'From the birth of the Great Ultimate came earth and heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when purpose reaches its utmost, things respond; when thought is refined, the Way arrives. I praise your earnest labor without idle chatter, and will compose a hymn for you, saying: 'From the birth of the Great Ultimate came earth and heaven.

sentences.zh: 中含五精，五精之用而水居一焉。

translations.literal: Within them were contained the five essences; among the workings of the five essences, water holds one place.
translations.idiomatic: Within them lay the five essences; among the workings of the five essences, water holds one place.

sentences.zh: 水之疏，邇則為江兮，遠則為河；

translations.literal: When water flows forth, near at hand it becomes rivers; far away it becomes the great river;
translations.idiomatic: When water spreads abroad, near at hand it becomes rivers; far away it becomes the Yellow River;

sentences.zh: 積則為瀦兮，總則為湖。

translations.literal: where it gathers it becomes marshes; where it collects it becomes lakes.
translations.idiomatic: where it pools it becomes marshes; where it gathers altogether it becomes lakes.

sentences.zh: 若今所謂洞庭者，傑立而孤，廓然如無區，其大無徒。

translations.literal: As for what is now called Dongting—it stands towering and alone, vast as though without boundary, so great it has no peer.
translations.idiomatic: As for what is now called Dongting—it rears up solitary and grand, boundless as though without quarter, so vast it has no equal.

sentences.zh: 含陽字陰，玄神之都。

translations.literal: It holds yang and orders yin, a capital of the dark divine.
translations.idiomatic: It embraces yang and arrays yin, a capital of the dark divine.

sentences.zh: 曖曖昧昧，百川不敢逾。

translations.literal: Dim and hidden, a hundred streams dare not cross it.
translations.idiomatic: Dim and obscure, a hundred streams dare not cross it.

sentences.zh: 有若臣者，有若賓者，有若仆者，有若子者，有若附庸者，有若娣姒者。

translations.literal: Some are like ministers, some like guests, some like servants, some like sons, some like vassals, some like sisters-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Some are like ministers, some like guests, some like servants, some like sons, some like vassals, some like sisters-in-law.

sentences.zh: 若禹會塗山，武巡牧野，千出百會，咸處麾下。

translations.literal: As when Yu assembled at Mount Tu and King Wu marched through Muye—thousands issuing forth, hundreds converging, all under its command.
translations.idiomatic: As when Yu assembled at Mount Tu and King Wu reviewed the field at Muye—thousands issuing forth, hundreds converging, all arrayed beneath its command.

sentences.zh: 每六合澄靜，中流回睨。

translations.literal: Whenever the six directions grow clear and still, it turns a backward glance from midstream.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the six directions grow clear and still, it turns a backward glance from midstream.

sentences.zh: 莽莽蒼蒼，纖靄不翳。

translations.literal: Boundless and blue-green, the finest mists cannot veil it.
translations.idiomatic: Boundless and blue-green, the finest mists cannot shroud it.

sentences.zh: 太陽望舒，出沒其間。

translations.literal: The sun and Wangshu, rising and setting, pass through it.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and the moon, rising and setting, pass through it.

sentences.zh: 萬頃咸沸，強而名之為巨澤，為長川，為水府，為大淵。

translations.literal: Ten thousand acres all seething—one must force names upon it: Great Marsh, Long River, Palace of Waters, Grand Abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand acres all seething—one must force names upon it: Great Marsh, Long River, Palace of Waters, Grand Abyss.

sentences.zh: 縱之不逾，忠心之不卑。

translations.literal: Release it and it does not overstep; confine it and it does not grow abject.
translations.idiomatic: Release it and it does not overstep; confine it and it does not grow abject.

sentences.zh: 乍若賢人，以重自持。

translations.literal: At times like a worthy man, holding himself by weight and dignity.
translations.idiomatic: At times like a worthy man, holding himself by weight and dignity.

sentences.zh: 誘之不前，犯之愈堅。

translations.literal: Lure it and it will not advance; assail it and it grows ever firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Lure it and it will not advance; assail it and it grows ever firmer.

sentences.zh: 又若良將，以謀守邊。

translations.literal: Again like a fine general, guarding the frontier by strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Again like a fine general, guarding the frontier by strategy.

sentences.zh: 澎澎濞濞，浩爾一致。

translations.literal: Surging and billowing, vast and of one accord.
translations.idiomatic: Surging and billowing, vast and of one accord.

sentences.zh: 又若太始，未有仁義。

translations.literal: Again like primordial beginning, before benevolence and righteousness existed.
translations.idiomatic: Again like primordial beginning, before benevolence and righteousness existed.

sentences.zh: 衝訓漠漠，二氣交錯。

translations.literal: Churning and boundless, the two breaths interweave.
translations.idiomatic: Churning and boundless, the two breaths interweave.

sentences.zh: 又若混沌，凝然未鑿。

translations.literal: Again like chaos, solidified and yet unshaped.
translations.idiomatic: Again like chaos, solidified and yet unshaped.

sentences.zh: 此乃方輿之心胸，溟海之郛郭也。

translations.literal: This is the breast of the square earth, the outer wall of the dark sea.
translations.idiomatic: This is the breast of the square earth, the outer rampart of the dark sea.

sentences.zh: 三代之前，其氣落。

translations.literal: Before the Three Dynasties, its breath ran wild.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Three Dynasties, its breath ran wild.

sentences.zh: 浩浩滔天，與物回薄。

translations.literal: Roaring to the skies, rolling with all things.
translations.idiomatic: Roaring to the skies, rolling with all things.

sentences.zh: 滅木襄陵，無際無廓。

translations.literal: Drowning trees and swamping hills, without limit or margin.
translations.idiomatic: Drowning trees and swamping hills, without limit or margin.

sentences.zh: 上帝降鑒，巨人斯作。

translations.literal: The Supreme Lord sent down his regard, and the giant arose.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Lord sent down his regard, and the giant arose.

sentences.zh: 乃命玄夷，授禹之機。
