translations.literal: He commanded Xuan Yi and entrusted Yu with the secret mechanism.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Xuan Yi and entrusted Yu with the secret mechanism.

sentences.zh: 隧山陻谷，滌源暢微。

translations.literal: He cut through mountains and filled valleys, cleared the sources and opened the subtle channels.
translations.idiomatic: He cut through mountains and filled valleys, cleared the sources and opened the subtle channels.

sentences.zh: 然後若金在熔，若木在工，流精成器，夫何不通。

translations.literal: Then, as metal in the smelting, as wood in the craftsman's hands, flowing essence became vessels—how could anything remain blocked?
translations.idiomatic: Then, as metal in the smelting, as wood in the craftsman's hands, flowing essence became vessels—how could anything remain blocked?

sentences.zh: 是澤之設，允執厥中。

translations.literal: Thus this marsh was established, truly holding the center.
translations.idiomatic: Thus this marsh was established, truly holding the center.

sentences.zh: 既巽其性，遂得其正。

translations.literal: Once its nature was made yielding, it attained its proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Once its nature was made yielding, it attained its proper order.

sentences.zh: 有升有降，有動有靜。』」

translations.literal: It has rising and falling, movement and stillness.'"
translations.idiomatic: It has rising and falling, movement and stillness.'"

sentences.zh: 臣應之曰：「升降動靜，可得聞乎？」

translations.literal: The minister replied: "Rising, falling, movement, and stillness—might I hear of them?
translations.idiomatic: The minister replied, "Rising, falling, movement, and stillness—might I hear of them?

sentences.zh: 神曰：「水之性非圓非方，非柔非剛，非直非曲，非玄非黃。

translations.literal: The spirit said: "Water's nature is neither round nor square, neither soft nor hard, neither straight nor curved, neither black nor yellow.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit said, "Water's nature is neither round nor square, neither soft nor hard, neither straight nor curved, neither black nor yellow.

sentences.zh: 劃象為《坎》，本乎羲皇。

translations.literal: It was traced as the hexagram 《Kan》, rooted in the reign of Fuxi.
translations.idiomatic: It was traced as the hexagram 《Kan》, rooted in the age of Fuxi.

sentences.zh: 外婉而固，內健而彰。

translations.literal: Outwardly gentle yet firm, inwardly strong and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly gentle yet firm, inwardly strong and manifest.

sentences.zh: 降以《後》始，升以《復》張。

translations.literal: Its descent begins with 《Gou》; its ascent spreads with 《Fu》.
translations.idiomatic: Its lowering begins with 《Gou》; its rising opens with 《Fu》.

sentences.zh: 其靜處陰，其動隨陽。

translations.literal: In stillness it rests in yin; in movement it follows yang.
translations.idiomatic: In stillness it rests in yin; in movement it follows yang.

sentences.zh: 六府之甲，萬化之綱。

translations.literal: Chief among the six storehouses, the guiding cord of ten thousand transformations.
translations.idiomatic: Chief among the six storehouses, the guiding cord of ten thousand transformations.

sentences.zh: 式觀是澤，乃知天常。

translations.literal: Observe this marsh and you may know heaven's constant way.
translations.idiomatic: Observe this marsh and you may know heaven's constant way.

sentences.zh: 若乃四序之變，九夏攸處。

translations.literal: As for the turnings of the four seasons, the height of midsummer.
translations.idiomatic: As for the turnings of the four seasons, the height of midsummer.

sentences.zh: 烘然而炎，沸然而煮。

translations.literal: Blazing hot, boiling as if in a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Blazing hot, boiling as if in a cauldron.

sentences.zh: 群物鴻洞，爍為隆暑。

translations.literal: All creatures swim in vast profusion, blazing into deepest summer heat.
translations.idiomatic: All creatures swim in vast profusion, blazing into deepest summer heat.

sentences.zh: 澤之作，頎然其容，若去若住，若茹若吐。

translations.literal: When the marsh stirs, its aspect grows tall—seeming to go yet seeming to stay, to swallow yet to spit forth.
translations.idiomatic: When the marsh stirs, its aspect grows tall—seeming to go yet seeming to stay, to swallow yet to spit forth.

sentences.zh: 靈趨怪覲，杳不可睹。

translations.literal: Spirits hurry and strange beings visit, too dim to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits hurry and strange beings visit, too dim to be seen.

sentences.zh: 蒸之為雲，散之為雨。

translations.literal: Steamed into clouds, dispersed into rain.
translations.idiomatic: Steamed into clouds, dispersed into rain.

sentences.zh: 倏急萬象，如還太古。

translations.literal: In a flash the ten thousand forms rush, as though returning to utmost antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In a flash the ten thousand forms rush, as though returning to utmost antiquity.

sentences.zh: 真可嘉也。

translations.literal: Truly it is worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Truly it is worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 若乃秋之為神，素氣清泚。

translations.literal: As for autumn's spirit, the plain breath runs clear and cold.
translations.idiomatic: As for autumn's spirit, the plain breath runs clear and cold.

sentences.zh: 肅肅翛閹，群籟四起。

translations.literal: Grave and whirling, a hundred sounds rise on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Grave and whirling, a hundred sounds rise on every side.

sentences.zh: 澤之動，黝然其姿，若挺若倚，若行若止，《巽》宮離離，為之騰風。

translations.literal: When the marsh moves, its form grows dark—now upright, now leaning, now walking, now halting; the palace of 《Xun》 stands scattered, whipping up wind for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the marsh moves, its form grows dark—now upright, now leaning, now walking, now halting; the palace of 《Xun》 stands scattered, whipping up wind for it.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧崇崇，為之供雲。

translations.literal: Cangwu towers high, supplying it with clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Cangwu towers high, supplying it with clouds.

sentences.zh: 四顧一色，黯然氤氳。

translations.literal: Looking on every side, one color alone—dim and thick with mist.
translations.idiomatic: Looking on every side, one color alone—dim and thick with mist.

sentences.zh: 其聲瀰瀰，若商非商，若徵非徵。

translations.literal: Its sound rolls on and on, like the note shang yet not shang, like zhi yet not zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Its sound rolls on and on, like the note shang yet not shang, like zhi yet not zhi.

sentences.zh: 東湊海門，一浪千里。

translations.literal: It gathers eastward at the sea gate, one wave for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: It gathers eastward at the sea gate, one wave for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 又足畏也。

translations.literal: Again, it is truly awesome.
translations.idiomatic: Again, it is truly awesome.

sentences.zh: 言其狀，則石然而骨，岸然而革。

translations.literal: To speak of its form: stony in bone, shore-like in hide.
translations.idiomatic: To speak of its form: stony in bone, shore-like in hide.

sentences.zh: 氣然而榮，洚然而脈。

translations.literal: Breathing yet luxuriant, flood-deep yet pulsing.
translations.idiomatic: Breathing yet luxuriant, flood-deep yet pulsing.

sentences.zh: 有山而心，有洞而腹。

translations.literal: With mountains for its heart, caverns for its belly.
translations.idiomatic: With mountains for its heart, caverns for its belly.

sentences.zh: 有玉而體，有珠而目。

translations.literal: Jade for its body, pearls for its eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Jade for its body, pearls for its eyes.

sentences.zh: 穹鼻孤島，呀口萬谷。

translations.literal: Its arched snout is a lone isle; its gaping mouth, ten thousand valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Its arched snout is a lone isle; its gaping mouth, ten thousand valleys.

sentences.zh: 臂帶三吳，足跬荊、巫。

translations.literal: Its arms girdle the Three Wu; its feet stand a pace from Jing and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Its arms girdle the Three Wu; its feet stand a pace from Jing and Wu.

sentences.zh: 或跂然而望，或翼然而趨。

translations.literal: Some stand on tiptoe and gaze; some spread wings and hasten.
translations.idiomatic: Some stand on tiptoe and gaze; some spread wings and hasten.

sentences.zh: 彭蠡、震澤，詎可云乎？」

translations.literal: Can Pengli and Zhenze even be mentioned in the same breath?"
translations.idiomatic: Can Pengli and Zhenze even be mentioned in the same breath?"

sentences.zh: 臣又問曰：「澤之態已聞命矣。

translations.literal: The minister asked again: "I have heard your command concerning the marsh's mien.
translations.idiomatic: The minister asked again, "I have heard your command concerning the marsh's mien.

sentences.zh: 水之族將如何居？」

translations.literal: How do the tribes of the water dwell within it?
translations.idiomatic: How do the tribes of the water dwell within it?

sentences.zh: 神曰：「大道變易，或文或質。

translations.literal: The spirit said: "The Great Way shifts and changes—sometimes refined, sometimes plain.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit said, "The Great Way shifts and changes—sometimes refined, sometimes plain.

sentences.zh: 沉潛自遂，其類非一。

translations.literal: They sink and plunge as each finds its way; their kinds are not one.
translations.idiomatic: They sink and plunge as each finds its way; their kinds are not one.

sentences.zh: 或被甲而，或曳裾而圓。

translations.literal: Some wear armor and move with deliberate pace; some trail skirts and wheel in circles.
translations.idiomatic: Some wear armor and move with deliberate pace; some trail skirts and wheel in circles.

sentences.zh: 或禿而跂，或角而蜿。

translations.literal: Some bald and striding; some horned and winding.
translations.idiomatic: Some bald and striding; some horned and winding.

sentences.zh: 或吞而呀，或去而牙。

translations.literal: Some swallow with gaping mouths; some baring fangs wide.
translations.idiomatic: Some swallow with gaping mouths; some baring fangs wide.

sentences.zh: 或心以之蟹，或目以之蝦。

translations.literal: Some take the crab for a heart; some take the shrimp for eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Some take the crab for a heart; some take the shrimp for eyes.

sentences.zh: 或修臂而立，或橫騖而疾。

translations.literal: Some stand on long arms; some gallop sideways in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Some stand on long arms; some gallop sideways in haste.

sentences.zh: 或發於首，或髯於肘。

translations.literal: Some bristle from the head; some grow beards upon the elbows.
translations.idiomatic: Some bristle from the head; some grow beards upon the elbows.

sentences.zh: 或儼而莊，或毅而黝。

translations.literal: Some stern and dignified; some fierce and dark.
translations.idiomatic: Some stern and dignified; some fierce and dark.

sentences.zh: 彪彪玢玢，若大虛之含萬彙，名循其生而合乎群者也。」

translations.literal: Striped and mottled, bright and dappled, as though the great void held ten thousand forms—each follows its birth and finds its place among the flock."
translations.idiomatic: Striped and mottled, bright and dappled, as though the great void held ten thousand forms—each follows its birth and finds its place among the flock."

sentences.zh: 臣又問曰：「若神之資，其品何如也？」

translations.literal: The minister asked again: "As for a spirit's endowments, what is their rank and quality?
translations.idiomatic: The minister asked again, "As for a spirit's endowments, what is their rank and quality?

sentences.zh: 神曰：「清矣靜矣，麗矣至矣，邈難知矣。

translations.literal: The spirit said: "Pure, tranquil, beautiful, utmost—and far beyond knowing.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit said, "Pure, tranquil, beautiful, utmost—and far beyond knowing.

sentences.zh: 肇於古，古有所未達；

translations.literal: Born from antiquity, yet antiquity had not fully grasped them;
translations.idiomatic: Born from antiquity, yet antiquity had not fully grasped them;

sentences.zh: 形於今，今有所未察。

translations.literal: taking form in the present, yet the present has not fully discerned them.
translations.idiomatic: taking form in the present, yet the present has not fully discerned them.

sentences.zh: 非希夷合其心於自然，然後上天入地，把三根六。

translations.literal: Only one who, like Xi Yi, unites his heart with nature may then ascend to heaven and enter earth, grasp the three roots and six limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Only one who, like Xi Yi, unites his heart with nature may then ascend to heaven and enter earth, grasp the three roots and six limbs.

sentences.zh: 況水居陸處，夫何不燭。

translations.literal: How much less when dwelling in water or on land—is there anything their light does not reach?
translations.idiomatic: How much less when dwelling in water or on land—is there anything their light does not reach?

sentences.zh: 彼鞚鯉之賢，轡龍之仙，乃吾之肩也。

translations.literal: Those sages who mounted carp and bridled dragons—they alone are fit to stand shoulder to shoulder with me.
translations.idiomatic: Those sages who mounted carp and bridled dragons—they alone are fit to stand shoulder to shoulder with me.

sentences.zh: 其餘海若、天吳，陽侯、神胥，齪齪而遊，曾不我儔。」

translations.literal: As for the rest—Hairuo, Tianwu, Yanghou, Shenxu—they scrabble about in their narrow rounds and are not fit to be my peers."
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest—Hairuo, Tianwu, Yanghou, Shenxu—they scrabble about in their narrow rounds and are not fit to be my peers."

sentences.zh: 臣又問曰：「《易》稱『王公設險』，是澤之險可以為固。

translations.literal: The minister asked again: "The 《Yi》 says, 'Kings and dukes establish defenses'—the peril of this marsh might serve as a bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: The minister asked again, "The 《Yi》 says, 'Kings and dukes establish defenses'—the peril of this marsh might serve as a bulwark.

sentences.zh: 而歷代興衰，其義安取？」

translations.literal: Yet through the rise and fall of dynasties, what lesson is to be drawn?
translations.idiomatic: Yet through the rise and fall of dynasties, what lesson is to be drawn?

sentences.zh: 神曰：「天道以順不以逆，地道以謙不以盈。

translations.literal: The spirit said: "Heaven's Way favors accord, not rebellion; earth's way favors modesty, not fullness.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit said, "Heaven's Way favors accord, not rebellion; earth's way favors modesty, not fullness.

sentences.zh: 故治理之世，建仁為旌，聚心為城。

translations.literal: Thus in ages of good rule, benevolence is raised as a banner and united hearts become the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in ages of good rule, benevolence is raised as a banner and united hearts become the wall.

sentences.zh: 而弧不暇弦，矛不暇鋒，四海以之而大同。

translations.literal: Bows need not be strung nor spears whetted, and the four seas thereby reach great unity.
translations.idiomatic: Bows need not be strung nor spears whetted, and the four seas thereby reach great unity.

sentences.zh: 何必恃險阻，何必據要衝？

translations.literal: Why must one rely on steep passes? Why must one hold strategic crossroads?
translations.idiomatic: Why must one rely on steep passes? Why must one hold strategic crossroads?

sentences.zh: 若秦得百二為帝，齊得十二而王。

translations.literal: As Qin with its hundred-and-two passes became emperor, and Qi with its twelve gates became king.
translations.idiomatic: As Qin with its hundred-and-two passes became emperor, and Qi with its twelve gates became king.

sentences.zh: 其山為金，其水為湯。

translations.literal: Their mountains were ore, their waters boiling springs—
translations.idiomatic: Their mountains were ore, their waters boiling springs—

sentences.zh: 守之不義，然而亡。

translations.literal: yet held without righteousness, they perished all the same.
translations.idiomatic: yet held without righteousness, they perished all the same.

sentences.zh: 水不在大，恃之者敗。

translations.literal: It is not that water's size matters; those who lean upon it are ruined.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that water's size matters; those who lean upon it are ruined.

sentences.zh: 水不在微，怙之者危。

translations.literal: Nor that water's meagerness matters; those who depend on it blindly face danger.
translations.idiomatic: Nor that water's meagerness matters; those who depend on it blindly face danger.

sentences.zh: 若漢疲於昆明，桀困於酒池，亦其類也。

translations.literal: As Han exhausted itself over the Kunming Pool, and Jie was trapped by his Wine Pool—these belong to the same class of folly.
translations.idiomatic: As Han exhausted itself over the Kunming Pool, and Jie was trapped by his Wine Pool—these belong to the same class of folly.

sentences.zh: 故黃帝張樂而興，三苗棄義而傾。

translations.literal: Thus the Yellow Emperor spread music and flourished, while the Three Miao forsook righteousness and fell.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Yellow Emperor spread music and flourished, while the Three Miao forsook righteousness and fell.

translations.literal: Then one knows that the waves of Dongting are governed by benevolence and not by disorder, by the Way and not by brigandage—only the worthy, observing its wisdom, can afterward grasp this."
translations.idiomatic: Then one knows that Dongting's waters are ruled by benevolence, not chaos, by the Way, not by violence—only the worthy, discerning its wisdom, can truly understand."

sentences.zh: 於是盤桓徙倚，凝精流視。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lingered and paced about, fixing his spirit in a flowing gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he lingered and paced, his spirit fixed in a flowing gaze.

sentences.zh: 罄以辭對，倏然而晦。

translations.literal: He exhausted words in reply, and suddenly it grew dark.
translations.idiomatic: He exhausted his words in reply, and suddenly all grew dark.

sentences.zh: 徐鉉見之，曰：「是玄虛之流也。」

translations.literal: Xu Xuan saw it and said: "This belongs to the school of arcane mystery."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan read it and said, "This is the sort of writing that traffics in arcane mystery."

sentences.zh: 人多傳寫。

translations.literal: Many people copied and circulated it.
translations.idiomatic: Many people copied and circulated it.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，太宗知其名，召試辭賦，擢為右正言、直史館兼直秘閣，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duangong era, Emperor Taizong knew his name, summoned him to test literary composition, promoted him to Right Rectifier, Direct Historiographer with concurrent Directorship of the Secret Pavilion, and bestowed a crimson fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Duangong era, Emperor Taizong knew his reputation, summoned him to test his prose and poetry, and promoted him to Right Rectifier, Direct Historiographer with concurrent Directorship of the Secret Pavilion, bestowing a crimson fish tally.

sentences.zh: 元夕，上御乾元門觀燈，嘉正獻五言十韻詩，其末句云：「兩製誠堪羨，青雲侍玉輿。」

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival night the emperor attended at Qianyuan Gate to view the lamps. Jiazheng presented a pentasyllabic poem of ten rhymes, whose closing lines read: "Both secretariat posts are truly enviable— amid azure clouds attending the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: On Lantern Festival night the emperor went to Qianyuan Gate to view the lamps. Jiazheng presented a pentasyllabic poem in ten rhymes whose closing lines read, "Both Hanlin posts are truly enviable— amid azure clouds attending the jade carriage."

sentences.zh: 上依韻和以賜之，有「狹劣終雖舉，通才列上居」之句，議者以為誡嘉正之好進也。

translations.literal: The emperor replied in matching rhyme and bestowed it, including the lines "Though narrow and inferior, in the end you are raised; the broadly talented take the upper place." Commentators held this was a warning to Jiazheng for his eagerness to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied in matching rhyme and bestowed his poem, including the lines "Though narrow and petty, in the end you are raised; the broadly talented take the higher place." Commentators took this as a rebuke of Jiazheng's eagerness to advance.

sentences.zh: 未幾被病，詔以為益王生辰使。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill. An edict appointed him birthday envoy to Prince Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill. An edict appointed him birthday envoy to Prince Yi.

sentences.zh: 所獲金幣，鬻得錢輦歸家，忽一緡自地起立，良久而仆，聞者異之。

translations.literal: The gold and coins he received he sold for cash and carted home. Suddenly one string of cash rose from the ground, stood a long while, then fell—hearers found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: The gold and coins he received he sold for cash and carted home. Suddenly one string of cash rose from the ground, stood upright a long while, then toppled over—those who heard of it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 嘉正疾遂篤，月餘卒，年三十七。

translations.literal: Jiazheng's illness grew grave; after more than a month he died at age thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazheng's illness grew grave, and after more than a month he died at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子紓，太子中舍。

translations.literal: His son Shu was a Palace Attendant in the Crown Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu served as a Palace Attendant in the Crown Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 羅處約，字思純，益州華陽人，唐酷吏希奭之裔孫。

translations.literal: Luo Chuyue, styled Sichun, came from Huayang in Yizhou. He was a descendant of Xi Yi, the Tang dynasty's notorious harsh official.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Chuyue, styled Sichun, was a native of Huayang in Yizhou and a descendant of Xi Yi, the Tang dynasty's notorious harsh official.

sentences.zh: 伯祖袞，唐末為諫官。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Gun served as a remonstrating official at the end of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Gun served as a remonstrating official in the late Tang.

sentences.zh: 父濟，仕蜀為升朝官。

translations.literal: His father Ji served Shu as an official attending court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji served Shu as an official qualified to attend court at the capital.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，至太常丞。

translations.literal: After submitting to the Song court he rose to Assistant Director of the Imperial Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting to the Song court he rose to Assistant Director of the Imperial Music Office.

sentences.zh: 處約嘗作《黃老先六經論》，曰：

translations.literal: Chuyue once wrote 《On Huang-Lao Preceding the Six Classics》, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chuyue once wrote 《On Huang-Lao Preceding the Six Classics》, which says:

sentences.zh: 先儒以太史公論道德，先黃、老而後《六經》，此其所以病也。

translations.literal: Earlier Confucians fault Grand Historian Sima Qian's discussion in the Treatise on the Way of Heaven for placing Huang-Lao before the 《Six Classics》—that is what they criticize.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Confucians faulted Grand Historian Sima Qian's Treatise on the Way of Heaven for placing Huang-Lao before the 《Six Classics》—that is their objection.

sentences.zh: 某曰：「不然，道者何？

translations.literal: I say: "Not so. What is the Way?
translations.idiomatic: I say, "Not so. What is the Way?

sentences.zh: 無之稱也，無不由也。

translations.literal: It is a name for Nothingness; nothing does not proceed through it.
translations.idiomatic: It is a name for the formless; nothing exists that does not proceed through it.

sentences.zh: 混成而仙，兩儀至虛而應萬物，不可致詰。

translations.literal: Formed from chaos into the sublime, the two powers are utterly empty yet respond to the ten thousand things—this cannot be pursued to interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Blended from chaos into the sublime, the two powers are utterly empty yet answer the ten thousand things—this cannot be pursued to the end by questioning.

sentences.zh: 況名之曰『道』，道既名矣，降而為聖人者，為能知來藏往，與天地準，故黃、老、姬、孔通稱焉。

translations.literal: Moreover, once it is named 'the Way' and the Way has received a name, those who descend to become sages can know what is coming and conceal what has passed and align with Heaven and Earth—hence Huang, Lao, Ji, and Confucius are all honored by the same title.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, once it is named 'the Way,' those who descend to become sages can know what is coming and hold what has passed, aligning themselves with Heaven and Earth—hence Huangdi, Laozi, the house of Ji, and Confucius are all honored by the same title.

sentences.zh: 其體曰道，其用曰神，無適也，無莫也，一以貫之，胡先而尊，孰後而愧。」

translations.literal: Its substance is called the Way, its function called spirit—it has nowhere it does not reach, nothing it does not pervade. One thread runs through all—why honor one first and leave another ashamed to follow?"
translations.idiomatic: Its substance is called the Way, its function called spirit—it reaches everywhere and pervades all things. One thread runs through them—why should one be honored first and another left ashamed to follow?"

sentences.zh: 「《六經》者，《易》以明人之權而本之於道；

translations.literal: "The 《Six Classics》: the 《Changes》 reveals human discretion while grounding it in the Way;
translations.idiomatic: "The 《Six Classics》: the 《Changes》 clarifies human discretion while grounding it in the Way;

sentences.zh: 《禮》以節民之情，趣於性也；

translations.literal: the 《Rites》 restrains the people's emotions, guiding them toward nature;
translations.idiomatic: the 《Rites》 restrains the people's emotions and guides them toward their nature;

sentences.zh: 《樂》以和民之心，全天真也；

translations.literal: the 《Music》 harmonizes the people's hearts, completing innate truth;
translations.idiomatic: the 《Music》 harmonizes the people's hearts and completes their innate truth;

sentences.zh: 《書》以敘九疇之秘，煥二帝之美；

translations.literal: the 《Documents》 narrates the secret of the Nine Categories and brings forth the glory of the Two Emperors;
translations.idiomatic: the 《Documents》 recounts the secret of the Nine Categories and brings forth the glory of the Two Emperors;

sentences.zh: 《春秋》以正君臣而敦名教；

translations.literal: the 《Spring and Autumn》 rectifies lord and minister and reinforces the teaching of names;
translations.idiomatic: the 《Spring and Autumn》 rectifies the relation of lord and minister and strengthens the teaching of names;

sentences.zh: 《詩》以正風雅而存規戒。

translations.literal: the 《Odes》 corrects the feng and ya styles and preserves admonition.
translations.idiomatic: the 《Odes》 corrects the feng and ya styles and preserves admonition.

sentences.zh: 是道與《六經》一也。」

translations.literal: Thus the Way and the 《Six Classics》 are one."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Way and the 《Six Classics》 are one."

sentences.zh: 「矧仲尼祖述堯、舜，則況於帝鴻氏乎？

translations.literal: "Moreover, since Confucius traced his lineage to Yao and Shun, how much more should this apply to the Emperor Hong?
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, since Confucius traced his teaching to Yao and Shun, how much more should this apply to the Emperor Hong?

sentences.zh: 華胥之治，太上之德，史傳詳矣。

translations.literal: The governance of Huaxu and the virtue of the Supreme Lord are fully recorded in histories.
translations.idiomatic: The governance of Huaxu and the virtue of the Supreme Lord are fully recorded in the histories.

sentences.zh: 老聃世謂方外之教，然而與《六經》皆足以治國治身，清淨則得之矣。

translations.literal: Laozi is called a teaching outside the world, yet it and the 《Six Classics》 alike suffice to govern state and self—through clarity and stillness one attains this.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi is regarded as a teaching outside the world, yet both he and the 《Six Classics》 suffice to govern state and self—through clarity and stillness one attains this.

sentences.zh: 漢文之時，未遑學校，竇後以之而治，曹參得之而相，幾至措刑。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wen's time schools had not yet been established. Empress Dowager Dou governed by it, Cao Shen obtained it as chancellor, and punishments nearly fell into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wen's time schools had not yet been established. Empress Dowager Dou governed by it, Cao Shen mastered it as chancellor, and punishments nearly fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 且仲尼嘗問禮焉，俗儒或否其說。」

translations.literal: Moreover Confucius once inquired about rites from him. Pedantic Confucians sometimes reject this claim."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Confucius once inquired about rites from him, though pedantic Confucians sometimes reject this."

sentences.zh: 餘曰：「《春秋》昭十七年，郯子來朝，仲尼從而學焉，俾後之人敦好問之旨。

translations.literal: I say: "In the 《Spring and Autumn》, the seventeenth year of Duke Zhao, Lord Tan of Tan came to court. Confucius followed and learned from him, enabling later generations to honor the spirit of earnest inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: I say, "In the 《Spring and Autumn》, the seventeenth year of Duke Zhao, Lord Tan of Tan came to court. Confucius followed and learned from him, enabling later generations to honor the spirit of earnest inquiry.

sentences.zh: 矧老子有道之士，周之史氏乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, was Laozi not a man of the Way, a historiographer of Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, was Laozi not a man of the Way—a historiographer of Zhou?

sentences.zh: 餘謂《六經》之教，化而不已則臻於大同，大道之行則蠟賓息歎。

translations.literal: I hold that the teaching of the 《Six Classics》, when transformation continues without end, reaches great unity; when the Great Way is practiced, even Labin sighs and rests.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that when the teaching of the 《Six Classics》 transforms without cease it reaches great unity, and when the Great Way is practiced even distant Labin sighs and rests content.

sentences.zh: 黃、老之與《六經》，孰為先而孰為後乎？

translations.literal: Between Huang-Lao and the 《Six Classics》, which comes first and which after?
translations.idiomatic: Between Huang-Lao and the 《Six Classics》, which comes first and which after?

sentences.zh: 又何必繅藉玉帛然後為禮，筍虡鏞鼓然後為樂乎？

translations.literal: Why must silk and jade be reeled and laid out before there is rites, or reed frames, bell-stands, and drums before there is music?
translations.idiomatic: Why must silk and jade be laid out before there is rites, or reed frames, bell-stands, and great drums before there is music?

sentences.zh: 餘謂太史公之志，斯見之矣。

translations.literal: I say Grand Historian Sima's purpose is seen here.
translations.idiomatic: I say Grand Historian Sima's purpose is seen here.

sentences.zh: 惡可以道之跡、儒之末相戾而疾其說？

translations.literal: How can one, because the trace of the Way and the fringes of Confucianism diverge, despise his account?
translations.idiomatic: How can one despise his account merely because the trace of the Way and the fringes of Confucianism diverge?

sentences.zh: 病之者可以觀徼，未可以觀妙。」

translations.literal: Those who fault it may discern the outward trace, but not the inward mystery."
translations.idiomatic: Those who fault it may discern the outward trace, but not the inward mystery."

sentences.zh: 人多重之。

translations.literal: Many people valued it.
translations.idiomatic: Many people valued it.

sentences.zh: 登第，為臨渙主簿，再遷大理評事、知吳縣。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations, served as registrar of Linhuan, and was twice promoted to judicial reviewer and magistrate of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations, served as registrar of Linhuan, and was twice promoted to judicial reviewer and magistrate of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 王禹偁知長洲縣，日以詩什唱酬，蘇、杭間多傳誦。

translations.literal: Wang Yucheng was magistrate of Changzhou; day by day they exchanged verses, and many between Su and Hang circulated and recited them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yucheng was magistrate of Changzhou; day by day they exchanged verses in poetry, and their work was widely copied and recited between Suzhou and Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後並召赴闕，上自定題以試之，以禹偁為右拾遺，處約著作郎，皆直史館，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Later both were summoned to court. The emperor set topics himself to test them. Yucheng was made Right Reminder and Chuyue made Literary Scholar—both with direct appointment to the Historiography Institute and bestowal of crimson fish tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Later both were summoned to court. The emperor set the topics himself to test them, appointing Yucheng Right Reminder and Chuyue Literary Scholar—both with direct appointment to the Historiography Institute and the bestowal of crimson fish tallies.

sentences.zh: 會下詔求讜言，處約上奏曰：

translations.literal: When an edict was issued seeking frank counsel, Chuyue submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When an edict was issued seeking frank counsel, Chuyue submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 伏睹今年春詔旨，責以諫官備員未嘗言事，雖九寺、三監之官，亦得盡其讜議。

translations.literal: I have respectfully observed this spring's edict blaming remonstrating officials for filling posts yet not speaking—even officials of the nine directorates and three bureaus may fully offer frank counsel.
translations.idiomatic: I have respectfully observed this spring's edict rebuking remonstrating officials for holding posts yet never speaking—even officials of the nine directorates and three bureaus may fully offer frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 陛下虔恭勞神，厲精求理，力行王道，坐致太平。

translations.literal: Your Majesty devoutly and reverently labors in spirit, striving with rigor to seek good governance, earnestly practicing the royal Way, achieving peace while seated.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty devoutly labors in spirit, striving with rigor to seek good governance, earnestly practicing the royal Way and achieving peace without stirring from the throne.

sentences.zh: 心先天而不違，德生民而未有，所以散玄黃之協氣，為動植之休祥，而猶不伐功成，屢求獻替，此真唐堯、虞舜之用心也。

translations.literal: Your heart precedes Heaven without violating it; your virtue nurtures the people beyond anything yet seen—therefore dispersing the harmonizing breath of black and yellow, creating auspicious signs for the moving and rooted, and yet still not boasting of achievements, repeatedly seeking contributions and replacements—this is truly the spirit in which Tang Yao and Yu Shun applied themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Your heart precedes Heaven without violating it; your virtue nurtures the people beyond anything yet seen—therefore dispersing the harmonizing breath of black and yellow and bringing auspicious signs to the moving and rooted, and yet still not boasting of your achievements, repeatedly seeking counsel and reform—this is truly the spirit in which Tang Yao and Yu Shun applied themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣累日以來，趨朝之暇，或於卿士之內預聞時政之言，皆曰聖上以三司之中，邦計所屬，簿書既廣，綱條實繁，將求盡善之規，冀協酌中之道。

translations.literal: For several days recently in the intervals of attending court, I have occasionally heard current-affairs talk among ministers, all saying the sage emperor, regarding the Three Departments within which state revenue belongs—the account books are vast and regulations numerous—seeks a fully perfected plan, hoping to harmonize the middle way.
translations.idiomatic: For several days now, in the intervals of attending court, I have occasionally heard talk of current affairs among ministers, all saying that the sage emperor, regarding the Three Departments to which state revenue belongs—the account books are vast and the regulations numerous—seeks a fully perfected plan, hoping to harmonize the middle way.

sentences.zh: 竊聞省上言，欲置十二員判官兼領其職，貴各司其局，允執厥中。

translations.literal: I have heard it reported that the department proposes appointing twelve adjunct officials each to supervise duties, so each office handles its own business and truly holds the center.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it reported that the department proposes appointing twelve adjunct officials each to supervise their duties, so each office handles its own business and truly holds the center.

sentences.zh: 臣以三司之制非古也。

translations.literal: I hold that the Three Departments system is not ancient.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the Three Departments system is not ancient.

sentences.zh: 蓋唐朝中葉之後，兵寇相仍，河朔不王，軍旅未弭，以賦調筦榷之所出，故自尚書省分三司以董之。

translations.literal: It arose after the middle period of Tang, when warfare persisted in succession, the north of the Yellow River did not acknowledge royal rule, and military affairs were not settled. Because tax levies and monopoly revenues issued from there, the Ministry of Revenue was split into three departments to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: It arose after the middle Tang, when warfare persisted in succession, the north of the Yellow River did not acknowledge royal rule, and military affairs were not settled. Because tax levies and monopoly revenues issued from there, the Ministry of Revenue was split into three departments to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 然國用所須，朝廷急務，故僚吏之屬倚注尤深。

translations.literal: Yet what the state requires and what the court urgently needs—the subordinate officials are especially relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what the state requires and what the court urgently needs—the subordinate officials are especially relied upon.

sentences.zh: 或重其位以處之，優其祿以寵之，黽勉從事者姑務其因循，盡瘁事國者或生於睚眥，因循則無補於國，睚眥則不協於時。

translations.literal: Sometimes weighty posts are used to place them, generous salaries to favor them. Those who toil and comply merely maintain routine; those who exhaust their hearts for the state may provoke petty grudges. Routine brings no benefit to the state; petty grudges are incompatible with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes weighty posts are used to place them, generous salaries to favor them. Those who toil and comply merely maintain routine, while those who exhaust their hearts for the state may provoke petty grudges. Routine brings no benefit to the state; petty grudges are incompatible with the times.

sentences.zh: 或淺近之人用指瑕於心計，深識之士以多可為身謀。

translations.literal: Shallow men use finger-counting flaws in fiscal planning; deep thinkers use versatility as personal strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow men pick at flaws in fiscal planning, while deep thinkers use versatility as personal strategy.

sentences.zh: 蠹弊相沿，為日已久。

translations.literal: Corruption and abuse followed in succession for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Corruption and abuse have followed in succession for a long time.

sentences.zh: 今若如十二員判官之說，亦從權救敝之一端也。

translations.literal: Now if one follows the proposal of twelve adjunct officials, that too is merely one expedient for remedying abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Now if one follows the proposal of twelve adjunct officials, that too is merely one expedient for remedying abuse.

sentences.zh: 然而聖朝之政臻乎治平，當求稽古之規，以為垂世之法。

translations.literal: Yet the sage court's governance reaches order and peace—the time has come to seek regulations traced to antiquity as law for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sage court's governance has reached order and peace—the time has come to seek regulations traced to antiquity as law for generations.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗讀《說命》之書，以為「事不師古，匪說攸聞」又《二典》曰：「若稽古帝堯。」

translations.literal: I have read in the 《Announcement of Yue》, which says "He who does not model on the ancients will never hear the teaching of Fu Yue." Also the 《Two Canonical Documents》 say: "We examine antiquity with Emperor Yao."
translations.idiomatic: I have read in the 《Announcement of Yue》, which says, "He who does not model on the ancients will never hear the teaching of Fu Yue." The 《Two Canonical Documents》 also say, "We examine antiquity with Emperor Yao."

sentences.zh: 「若稽古帝舜。」

translations.literal: "We examine antiquity with Emperor Shun."
translations.idiomatic: "We examine antiquity with Emperor Shun."

sentences.zh: 皆謂順考古道而致治平。

translations.literal: All mean following and investigating ancient ways to achieve order and peace.
translations.idiomatic: All mean following and investigating ancient ways to achieve order and peace.

sentences.zh: 以臣所見，莫若復尚書都省故事，其尚書丞郎、正郎、員外郎、主事、令史之屬，請依六典舊儀。

translations.literal: In my view, nothing surpasses restoring the old practices of the consolidated Ministry. As for assistant ministers, directors, senior and junior clerks, chief clerks and recorders—please follow the ancient rites of the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, nothing surpasses restoring the old practices of the consolidated Ministry. As for assistant ministers, directors, senior and junior clerks, chief clerks, and recorders—please follow the ancient rites of the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 以今三司錢刀粟帛筦筦榷支度之事，均在二十四司，如此則各有司存，可以責其集事。

translations.literal: Put today's Three Departments matters of money, grain, silk, tolls, and disbursements all under the twenty-four offices—then each will have its proper charge and can be held accountable for gathering business.
translations.idiomatic: Put today's Three Departments matters of money, grain, silk, tolls, monopoly revenues, and disbursements all under the twenty-four offices—then each will have its proper charge and can be held accountable for completing its business.

sentences.zh: 今則金部、倉部安能知儲廩帑藏之盈虛，司田、司川孰能知屯役河渠之遠近？

translations.literal: As it is now, how can the Gold and Granary Sections know surfeit and shortage of storehouses and treasuries? Who among the Field and Water Offices can know the distance of garrison labor and canal works?
translations.idiomatic: As things stand, how can the Gold and Granary Sections know whether storehouses and treasuries run surplus or short? Who among the Field and Water Offices can know how far garrison labor and canal works extend?

sentences.zh: 有名無實，積久生常。

translations.literal: Names without substance, long accumulated become custom.
translations.idiomatic: Titles without substance, long accumulated, become custom.

sentences.zh: 況此卻復都省之事，下臣猶能僉知其可，況陛下聰明濬哲乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, if even this restoration of consolidated Ministry affairs is understood by low ministers like myself as feasible, how much more Your Majesty, wise and perspicacious!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if even this restoration of consolidated Ministry affairs is understood by low ministers like myself as feasible, how much more so for Your Majesty, wise and perspicacious!

sentences.zh: 然議者以為不行已久，難於改更，若斷自宸心，下於相府，都省之制，故典存焉。

translations.literal: Yet critics say it has not been practiced for long and would be hard to change. If Your Majesty decides from the depths of the throne and orders the chancellor's office—the consolidated Ministry system, the old statutes remain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet critics say it has not been practiced for long and would be hard to change. If Your Majesty decides from the depths of the throne and orders the chancellor's office, the consolidated Ministry system—the old statutes—still remain.

sentences.zh: 上令下從，孰為不可，蓋人者可與習常，難與適變；

translations.literal: When superiors command and inferiors follow, what cannot be done? Generally people can be accustomed to routine but have difficulty adapting to change;
translations.idiomatic: When superiors command and inferiors follow, what cannot be done? Generally people can be accustomed to routine but have difficulty adapting to change;

sentences.zh: 可與樂成，難與慮始。

translations.literal: they can rejoice at completion but have difficulty planning the start.
translations.idiomatic: they can rejoice at completion but have difficulty planning the start.

sentences.zh: 在《周易》有之：「天地革而四時成。」

translations.literal: It appears in the 《Book of Changes》: "Heaven and Earth revolve and the four seasons complete."
translations.idiomatic: It appears in the 《Book of Changes》: "Heaven and Earth revolve and the four seasons complete."

sentences.zh: 此言能改命而創製，及小人樂成則革麵以順上矣。

translations.literal: This means that when one can change destiny and create institutions, once petty men rejoice in completion they change their faces to follow superiors.
translations.idiomatic: This means that when one can change destiny and create institutions, once petty men rejoice in completion they change their faces to follow their superiors.

sentences.zh: 況三司之名興於近代，堆案盈幾之籍，何嘗能省覽之乎？

translations.literal: Moreover the name Three Departments arose in recent times—have the piled files heaping on desks ever truly been reviewed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the name Three Departments arose in recent times—have the piled files heaping on desks ever truly been reviewed?

sentences.zh: 復就三司之中，更分置僚屬，則愈失其本原矣。

translations.literal: To further divide and appoint subordinates within the Three Departments would lose the root principle all the more.
translations.idiomatic: To further divide and appoint subordinates within the Three Departments would lose the root principle all the more.

sentences.zh: 今三司勾院即尚書省，比部元為勾覆之司，周知內外經費，陛下若欲復之，則制度盡在。

translations.literal: Today's Three Departments auditing office is the old Ministry—the Audit Section was originally the verification office, comprehensively knowing internal and external expenditures. If Your Majesty wishes to restore it, the entire system remains intact.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Three Departments auditing office is the old Ministry—the Audit Section was originally the verification office, comprehensively knowing internal and external expenditures. If Your Majesty wishes to restore it, the entire system remains intact.

sentences.zh: 迨及九寺、三監多為冗長之司，雖有其民，不舉其職。

translations.literal: By then the nine directorates and three bureaus are largely redundant offices—though they have staffs, they do not perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: By then the nine directorates and three bureaus are largely redundant offices—though they have staffs, they do not perform their duties.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下當治平之日，建垂久之規，不煩更差使臣，別置公署。

translations.literal: I respectfully hope Your Majesty, in days of order and peace, will establish enduring regulations, not troubling to dispatch special envoys or set up separate offices.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully hope that in these days of order and peace Your Majesty will establish enduring regulations, without troubling to dispatch special envoys or set up separate offices.

sentences.zh: 如此則名正而言順，言順而事成，省其冗員則息其經費，故《書》曰：「唐虞稽古，建官惟百。

translations.literal: Then names would be correct and words accordant, words accordant and business accomplished. Reducing redundant staff would ease expenditures. Therefore the 《Documents》 says: "Tang and Yu examined antiquity and established one hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Then names would be correct and words accordant, words accordant and business accomplished. Reducing redundant staff would ease expenditures. Therefore the 《Documents》 says, "Tang and Yu examined antiquity and established one hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 夏、商官倍，亦克用乂。」

translations.literal: Xia and Shang doubled the offices, yet still could govern well."
translations.idiomatic: Xia and Shang doubled the offices, yet still could govern well."

sentences.zh: 伏望法天地簡易之化，建《洪範》大中之道，可以億萬斯年，垂衣裳而端拱矣。

translations.literal: I respectfully hope to follow the simplified transformation of Heaven and Earth and establish the great middle Way of the 《Grand Plan》, so the realm may endure ten thousand generations, draped in regal robes and seated in repose.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully hope to follow the simplified transformation of Heaven and Earth and establish the great middle Way of the 《Grand Plan》, so the realm may endure ten thousand generations, draped in regal robes and seated in repose.

sentences.zh: 受詔荊湖路巡撫，欲以苛察立名，所奏劾甚眾，官吏多被黜責。

translations.literal: He received orders as inspector of the Jing-Hu circuit, wishing to establish a reputation for harsh scrutiny—his impeachments were numerous and many officials were dismissed and punished.
translations.idiomatic: He received orders as inspector of the Jing-Hu circuit, wishing to establish a reputation for harsh scrutiny—his impeachments were numerous and many officials were dismissed and punished.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年卒，年三十三。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he died at age thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua he died at the age of thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 初，濟為開封府司錄，太宗尹京，頗嘉其強幹。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ji was chief clerk of the Kaifeng prefectural office, Taizong was prefect of the capital and greatly admired his strong competence.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ji was chief clerk of the Kaifeng prefectural office, Taizong was prefect of the capital and greatly admired his strong competence.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，處約與兄賁同舉進士，上臨試，知賁，濟之子，遂置之高等。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era Chuyue and his elder brother Ben both passed the jinshi together. When the emperor supervised the examination in person, recognizing Ben as Ji's son, he placed him in the highest rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era Chuyue and his elder brother Ben both passed the jinshi examination together. When the emperor supervised the examination in person and recognized Ben as Ji's son, he placed him in the highest rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，處約復登第。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Chuyue passed again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Chuyue passed the examination again.

sentences.zh: 賁後至員外郎。

translations.literal: Ben later reached outer desk officer.
translations.idiomatic: Ben later rose to outer desk officer.

sentences.zh: 處約形神豐碩，見者加重，雖有詞采而急於進用，時論亦以此薄之。

translations.literal: Chuyue was tall and imposing of form; those who saw him gave him extra weight. Though he had literary talent he was eager for advancement, and contemporary opinion likewise held this against him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyue was tall and imposing; those who saw him gave him extra weight. Though he had literary talent he was eager for advancement, and contemporary opinion likewise held this against him.

sentences.zh: 卒後，蘇易簡、王禹偁集其文凡十卷，題曰《東觀集》。

translations.literal: After his death Su Yijian and Wang Yucheng collected his writings in ten fascicles, titled 《Collected Writings of the Eastern Pavilion》.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Su Yijian and Wang Yucheng collected his writings in ten fascicles, titled 《Collected Writings of the Eastern Pavilion》.

sentences.zh: 禹偁為序，易簡表上之，詔付史館。

translations.literal: Yucheng wrote the preface, Yijian submitted it via memorial, and an edict ordered it delivered to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng wrote the preface, Yijian submitted it via memorial, and an edict ordered it delivered to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 蜀士又有嚴儲者，太平興國中進士，後直史館，使河北督軍糧，陷於契丹。

translations.literal: There was also a Shu scholar Yan Chu—jinshi in Taiping Xingguo, later direct historiographer, sent to Hebei to supervise military grain, captured by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Shu scholar named Yan Chu—a jinshi of the Taiping Xingguo era, later a direct historiographer, sent to Hebei to supervise military grain, and captured by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 安德裕，字益之，一字師皋，河南人。

translations.literal: An Deyu, styled Yizhi, also styled Shigao, came from Henan.
translations.idiomatic: An Deyu, styled Yizhi, also styled Shigao, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 父重榮，晉成德軍節度，《五代史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Chongrong was military governor of Chengde under Jin; the 《History of the Five Dynasties》 has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chongrong was military governor of Chengde under Jin; the 《History of the Five Dynasties》 contains his biography.

sentences.zh: 德裕生於真定，未期，重榮舉兵敗，乳母抱逃水竇中。

translations.literal: Deyu was born in Zhending. Before he was a year old Chongrong raised troops and was defeated. His wet nurse fled carrying him into a water culvert.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was born in Zhending. Before he was a year old Chongrong raised troops and was defeated. His wet nurse fled carrying him into a water culvert.

sentences.zh: 將出，為守兵所得，執以見軍校秦習，習與重榮有舊，因匿之。

translations.literal: As they emerged they were seized by garrison troops and brought before the military officer Qin Xi. Xi had old ties with Chongrong and therefore hid the child.
translations.idiomatic: As they emerged they were seized by garrison troops and brought before the military officer Qin Xi. Xi had old ties with Chongrong and therefore hid the child.

sentences.zh: 習先養石守瓊為子，及年壯無嗣，以德裕付瓊養之，因姓秦氏。

translations.literal: Xi had earlier raised Shi Shouqiong as his son; when he grew old without heirs he entrusted Deyu to Qiong to raise, and Deyu took the surname Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had earlier raised Shi Shouqiong as his son; when he grew old without heirs he entrusted Deyu to Qiong to raise, and Deyu took the surname Qin.

sentences.zh: 習世兵家，以弓矢、狗馬為事。

translations.literal: The Xi family were hereditary soldiers, their affairs bows, arrows, dogs, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi family were hereditary soldiers, occupied with bows, arrows, dogs, and horses.

sentences.zh: 德裕孩提即喜筆硯，遇文字輒為誦讀聲，諸子不之齒，習獨異之。

translations.literal: From childhood Deyu delighted in brush and inkstone; encountering writing he would recite aloud. The other sons did not regard him; Xi alone found him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Deyu delighted in brush and inkstone; whenever he encountered writing he would recite it aloud. The other sons did not regard him, but Xi alone found him unusual.

sentences.zh: 既成童，俾就學，遂博貫文史，精於《禮》、《傳》，嗜《西漢書》。

translations.literal: When he reached youth he was sent to study, and came to be broadly versed in literature and history, expert in the 《Rites》 and the 《Traditions》, and devoted to the 《Book of Han for the Western Han》.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached youth he was sent to study, and came to be broadly versed in literature and history, expert in the 《Rites》 and the 《Traditions》, and devoted to the 《Book of Han for the Western Han》.

sentences.zh: 習卒，德裕行三年服，然後還本姓。

translations.literal: When Xi died, Deyu observed three years of mourning, then restored his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi died, Deyu observed three years of mourning, then restored his original surname.

sentences.zh: 習家盡以橐裝與之，凡白金萬餘兩。

translations.literal: The Xi family gave him all their traveling funds, more than ten thousand taels of silver in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi family gave him all their traveling funds—more than ten thousand taels of silver in all.

sentences.zh: 德裕卻之，曰：「斯秦氏之蓄，於我何有？

translations.literal: Deyu refused, saying: "These are the Qin family's savings—what have they to do with me?
translations.idiomatic: Deyu refused, saying, "These are the Qin family's savings—what have they to do with me?

sentences.zh: 丈夫當自樹功名，以取富貴，豈屑於他人所有耶！」

translations.literal: A man should establish his own reputation and achieve wealth and rank through merit—why should he stoop to take what belongs to others!"
translations.idiomatic: A man should establish his own reputation and win wealth and rank through merit—why should he stoop to take what belongs to others!"

sentences.zh: 聞者高之。

translations.literal: Those who heard of it admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard of it admired him.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，擢進士甲科、歸州軍事推官，曆大理寺丞、著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he was selected jinshi with highest honors and appointed military judge of Guizhou; he served successively as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and assistant editor in the Bureau of Authorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he passed the jinshi examination with highest honors and was appointed military judge of Guizhou; he then served successively as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and assistant editor in the Bureau of Authorship.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，累遷秘書丞、知廣濟軍。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo he was repeatedly promoted to secretary of the Secretariat and military commissioner of Guangji Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo he was repeatedly promoted, serving as secretary of the Secretariat and military commissioner of Guangji Army.

sentences.zh: 時軍城新建，德裕作《軍記》及《圖經》三卷，優詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: At the time the garrison city was newly built; Deyu wrote the 《Military Record》 and three fascicles of the 《Gazetteer》, and received an edict of special commendation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the garrison city was newly built; Deyu wrote the 《Military Record》 and three fascicles of the 《Gazetteer》, and received an edict of special commendation.

sentences.zh: 俄改太常博士。

translations.literal: Soon after he was reassigned as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was reassigned as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 八年，通判秦州，就知州事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he became vice-prefect of Qinzhou and assumed the duties of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became vice-prefect of Qinzhou and assumed the duties of prefect.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，遷主客員外郎、通判廣州，未行，宰相李昉言其有史才，即以本官直史館。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongxi he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Receiving Guests and appointed vice-prefect of Guangzhou; before departing, Chief Councilor Li Fang cited his talent for history, and he was retained at his current rank as a direct historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongxi he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Receiving Guests and appointed vice-prefect of Guangzhou; before he could depart, Chief Councilor Li Fang cited his talent for history, and he was retained at his current rank as a direct historiographer.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改金部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，知開封縣，會備三館職，改直昭文館。

translations.literal: Early in Chunhua he governed Kaifeng county; when a vacancy arose among the Three Institutes he was reassigned as a direct contributor to the Hall of Spreading Culture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunhua he governed Kaifeng county; when a vacancy opened among the Three Institutes he was reassigned as a direct contributor to the Hall of Spreading Culture.

sentences.zh: 三年春，廷試貢士，德裕與史館修撰梁周翰並為考官，上顧宰相曰：「此皆有聞之士而老於郎署，周翰狹中，德裕嗜酒，朕聞其能改矣。」

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, at the palace examination of presented scholars, Deyu and the historiography institute compiler Liang Zhouhan served together as examiners. The emperor turned to his chief councilors and said: "These are both men of established reputation who have grown old in directorate posts—Zhouhan is narrow-minded, and Deyu is given to drink, but I hear he has reformed."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year, at the palace examination of presented scholars, Deyu and the historiography institute compiler Liang Zhouhan served together as examiners. The emperor turned to his chief councilors and said, "These are both men of established reputation who have grown old in directorate posts—Zhouhan is narrow-minded, and Deyu is given to drink, but I hear he has reformed."

sentences.zh: 遂並賜金紫。

translations.literal: Thereupon both were granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon both were granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 俄遷司勳員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Merits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Merits.

sentences.zh: 至道初，德裕常作《九弦琴五弦阮頌》以獻，上稱其詞采古雅。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhidao, Deyu composed and presented the 《Ode to the Nine-String Zither and Five-String Ruan》; the emperor praised its diction as classical and refined.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhidao, Deyu composed and presented the 《Ode to the Nine-String Zither and Five-String Ruan》; the emperor praised its diction as classical and refined.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，轉金部郎中、出知睦州，還判太府寺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao he was transferred to director of the Bureau of Revenue, sent out as prefect of Muzhou, then recalled to serve as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhidao he was transferred to director of the Bureau of Revenue, sent out as prefect of Muzhou, then recalled to serve as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Xianping, at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Xianping, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 德裕性介潔，以風鑒自負。

translations.literal: Deyu was upright and fastidious by nature, and prided himself on his judgment of character.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was upright and fastidious by nature, and prided himself on his judgment of character.

sentences.zh: 王禹偁、孫何皆初遊詞場，德裕力為延譽。

translations.literal: When Wang Yucheng and Sun He were first entering the literary arena, Deyu actively promoted their reputations.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yucheng and Sun He were first entering the literary arena, Deyu actively promoted their reputations.

sentences.zh: 及領考試，何又其首選。

translations.literal: When he later served as chief examiner, He was again his first choice.
translations.idiomatic: When he later served as chief examiner, He was again his first choice.

sentences.zh: 然酣飲太過，故不被獎擢。

translations.literal: Yet because he drank to excess he was never singled out for reward and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because he drank to excess he was never singled out for reward and promotion.

sentences.zh: 有集四十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works of forty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works of forty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 錢熙，字太雅，泉州南安人。

translations.literal: Qian Xi, styled Taiya, came from Nan'an in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xi, styled Taiya, was a native of Nan'an in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父居讓，陳洪進署清溪令。

translations.literal: His father Juren was appointed magistrate of Qingxi by Chen Hongjin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Juren was appointed magistrate of Qingxi by Chen Hongjin.

sentences.zh: 熙幼穎悟，及長，博貫群籍，善屬文，洪進嘉其才，以弟之子妻之。

translations.literal: Xi was precocious as a boy; when grown he mastered many texts and excelled at literary composition. Hongjin admired his talent and gave him his younger brother's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was precocious as a boy; when grown he mastered many texts and excelled at literary composition. Hongjin admired his talent and gave him his younger brother's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 將署熙府職，辭不就，著《楚鴈賦》以見志。

translations.literal: When Hongjin was about to appoint him to a post in his administration, Xi declined, and wrote the 《Rhapsody on the Chu Wild Goose》 to express his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjin was about to appoint him to a post in his administration, Xi declined and wrote the 《Rhapsody on the Chu Wild Goose》 to express his resolve.

sentences.zh: 尋復辟為巡官，專掌牋奏。

translations.literal: Soon he was again recruited as a patrol officer, exclusively drafting memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again recruited as a patrol officer, exclusively drafting memorials and reports.

sentences.zh: 洪進歸朝，熙不敘舊職，舉進士。

translations.literal: When Hongjin submitted to the court, Xi did not claim his former office and instead took the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjin submitted to the court, Xi did not claim his former office and instead took the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，攜文謁宰相李昉，昉深加賞重，為延譽於朝，令子宗諤與之遊。

translations.literal: Early in Yongxi he brought his writings to visit Chief Councilor Li Fang, who deeply admired them, promoted his reputation at court, and had his son Zong'e keep company with him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi he brought his writings to visit Chief Councilor Li Fang, who deeply admired them, promoted his reputation at court, and had his son Zong'e keep company with him.

sentences.zh: 明年，登甲科，補度州觀察推官。

translations.literal: The following year he passed with highest honors and was appointed observation bureau judge of Duzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed with highest honors and was appointed observation bureau judge of Duzhou.

sentences.zh: 代還，寇準掌吏部選，上封薦錢若水、陳充、王扶洎熙皆有文，得試中書，遷殿中丞，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: On returning from his term, Kou Zhun was in charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel; Xi submitted a sealed memorial recommending Qian Ruoshui, Chen Chong, Wang Fu, and himself as men of literary talent, all qualified for the Zhongshu examination; he was promoted to palace attendant and granted the red official robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his term, Kou Zhun was in charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel; Xi submitted a sealed memorial recommending Qian Ruoshui, Chen Chong, Wang Fu, and himself as men of literary talent, all qualified for the Zhongshu examination; he was promoted to palace attendant and granted the red official robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 著《四夷來王賦》以獻，凡萬餘言，太宗嘉之，即以本官直史館。

translations.literal: He composed and presented the 《Rhapsody on the Four Barbarians Coming to Court》, more than ten thousand characters in all; Emperor Taizong was pleased and immediately appointed him at his current rank as a direct historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: He composed and presented the 《Rhapsody on the Four Barbarians Coming to Court》, more than ten thousand characters in all; Emperor Taizong was pleased and immediately appointed him at his current rank as a direct historiographer.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，參知政事。

translations.literal: During Chunhua, Su Yijian was Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua, Su Yijian served as Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 蘇易簡對太宗言趙鄰幾追補《唐實錄》，鄰幾卒，家睢陽，即命熙乘傳而往，盡取其書來上。

translations.literal: Su Yijian told Taizong that Zhao Linji was continuing the 《Veritable Records of Tang》; when Linji died, his family was in Suiyang, and the emperor immediately ordered Xi to travel by relay post there and bring back all his manuscripts for submission.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yijian told Emperor Taizong that Zhao Linji was continuing the 《Veritable Records of Tang》; when Linji died, his family was in Suiyang, and the emperor immediately ordered Xi to travel by relay post there and bring back all his manuscripts for submission.

sentences.zh: 熙嘗與楊徽之言及張洎、錢若水將被進用，熙與劉昌言同鄉里，相親善，又語及其事。

translations.literal: Xi once told Yang Hui that Zhang Ji and Qian Ruoshui were about to receive appointment; Xi was from the same hometown as Liu Changyan and on close terms with him, and he also spoke of the matter to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi once told Yang Hui that Zhang Ji and Qian Ruoshui were about to receive appointment; Xi was from the same hometown as Liu Changyan and on close terms with him, and he also spoke of the matter to him.

sentences.zh: 昌言因以語洎，洎疑熙交構，訴之，熙坐削職、通判朗州，俄徙衡州，就改太常博士。

translations.literal: Changyan then told Ji; Ji suspected Xi of intrigue and lodged a complaint. Xi was demoted, made vice-prefect of Langzhou, soon transferred to Hengzhou, and then changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan then told Ji; Ji suspected Xi of sowing discord and lodged a complaint. Xi was demoted, made vice-prefect of Langzhou, soon transferred to Hengzhou, and then changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷右司諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, Xi was promoted to remonstrance officer of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong took the throne, Xi was promoted to remonstrance officer of the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李宗諤、楊億素厚善熙，乃與梁顥、趙況、趙安仁同表請復熙舊職，不報。

translations.literal: Li Zong'e and Yang Yi, who had long been close friends with Xi, joined Liang Hao, Zhao Kuang, and Zhao Anren in submitting a joint memorial asking that Xi's former office be restored; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zong'e and Yang Yi, who had long been close friends with Xi, joined Liang Hao, Zhao Kuang, and Zhao Anren in submitting a joint memorial asking that Xi's former office be restored; there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 尋通判杭州，政多專達，為轉運使所奏，徙通判越州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made vice-prefect of Hangzhou; his administration was often self-directed, and the transport commissioner reported him, so he was transferred as vice-prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made vice-prefect of Hangzhou; his administration was often self-directed, and the transport commissioner reported him, so he was transferred as vice-prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 熙負氣好學，善談笑，精筆劄，狷躁務進。

translations.literal: Xi was proud and studious, skilled at witty conversation, expert in brush correspondence, and impatient and ambitious for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was proud and studious, skilled at witty conversation, expert in brush correspondence, and impatient and ambitious for advancement.

sentences.zh: 自罷職，因憤恚成疾，咸平三年卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: From the time of his demotion, resentment and indignation brought on illness; he died in the third year of Xianping, at forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of his demotion, resentment and indignation brought on illness; he died in the third year of Xianping, at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 嘗擬古樂府，著《雜言》十數篇及《措刑論》，為識者所許。

translations.literal: He once modeled ancient yuefu, wrote more than ten pieces of 《Miscellaneous Words》 and the 《Essay on Abating Punishment》, praised by those with discernment.
translations.idiomatic: He once modeled ancient yuefu, wrote more than ten pieces of 《Miscellaneous Words》 and the 《Essay on Abating Punishment》, and was praised by those with discernment.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works of ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works of ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子蒙吉，亦進士及第。

translations.literal: His son Mengji also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mengji also passed the jinshi examination.
